In other words, over most of the disk, radial drift remains the dominant factor controlling the maximum dust size, and the magnetic field strength plays only a minor role in determining the overall dust size distribution.

papers.title: Operator generated topologies and the Krein property
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $σ(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $σ(X,Z)$-compact set is $σ(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $σ(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $σ(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $μ(X,Z)$ and $μ(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $μ(E^\odot,E)$ and $μ(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.

papers.title: Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincaré-type compactification, but a general theory was not established. Here, the two-dimensional ODE system derived by the linear chain trick is rewritten as an orbit equation, and a comparison theorem and an Osgood-type integral condition are applied to obtain a blow-up criterion based on the existence of a subsolution. This characterizes the nonlinearities for which memory-induced blow-up occurs. This paper also gives a necessary condition in a special case, a global existence condition based on a supersolution, and a systematic method for constructing subsolutions for separable nonlinearities. These results recover the author's previous results and are illustrated through several examples.

papers.title: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents
papers.abstract: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly deployed for long-running tasks that execute arbitrary shell commands or programs. However, these actions can result in unauthorized network requests or persistent, malicious changes to the user's file system, processes, or privileges. Existing defense mechanisms rely on either LLM-based monitors, which lack provable safety guarantees, or stateless policy enforcement layers, which miss multi-step data flows and execution side-effects unmodeled by the policy language (e.g., network calls initiated inside a Python script). We introduce Tether, a framework for runtime enforcement of stateful security policies over the observed side-effects of an agent's actions. Tether executes each proposed action in an ephemeral, isolated sandbox, inferring abstract action semantics from observed system calls. Tether then enforces stateful policies over these inferred semantics, permitting actions to proceed only if they comply with the policy. Policies and action semantics are defined in an embedded DSL in Lean 4 capable of expressing diverse constraints, including information flow control (IFC), access control, and network security policies. Because actions can propagate labels from sources to destinations, a single rule can enforce fine-grained IFC policies across multi-step execution flows of arbitrary length. Expressing policies in Lean enables formal verification that they satisfy global security invariants (e.g., preventing network access after reading a sensitive file). We evaluate Tether on realistic coding-agent benchmarks across both benign and adversarial trajectories. With a single policy shared across all tasks, Tether blocks 100% of in-scope attacks while maintaining a benign false-positive rate under 5%.

papers.title: Seamless Gradient Pixels for Multidimensional Optical Information Interrogation
papers.abstract: Information from light interaction with its environment can be extracted from its numerous properties. Yet capturing and interpreting this information within a single and compact platform remains challenging because conventional systems rely on discrete components and detection channels. Here we introduce the concept of "gradient pixels" that provides a universal metasurface platform to interrogate optical field information in the infrared (IR) spectrum. By continuously varying a design parameter across two dimensions, we encode multidimensional optical information into measurable spatial patterns, e.g., both spectral and polarization information are acquired from a single snapshot image. A free-form gradient pixel further enables prescribed wavelength-selective spatial patterns within a single metasurface through tailored gradient profiles. Unlike isolated filter arrays, seamless gradient-pixels multiplex neighbouring meta-atoms, increasing channel spatial density and relaxing Q-factor constraints. A 250-$μ$m footprint of these meta-atoms achieves spectral resolution better than 100-pm over a 100-nm spectral span based on a serpentine configuration. Snapshot wavelength-polarization reconstruction yields polarization angular accuracy at 0.3$^\circ$. We extend this concept to perform near-field refractive index sensing at video rates using the same explicit parameter-space mapping. By linking far-field detection and near-field sensing, it enables spatially resolved analysis of optical fields and local dielectric environments through a common image-based readout. It offers prospects for multidimensional optical sensing, computational imaging and intelligent information processing.

papers.title: Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as predictors across various tasks, benefiting from their ability to use information from unstructured context. However, when predictions serve as parameters of downstream optimization problems, higher prediction accuracy does not necessarily translate into lower decision costs. We propose decision-focused reinforcement learning (DFRL), a framework for post-training LLMs to predict optimization parameters using negative downstream decision regret as reward. DFRL trains LLM predictors to minimize the costs of the decisions induced by their predictions, without requiring downstream convexity or differentiability, and integrates readily into existing RL post-training frameworks. To address expensive reward evaluation, we develop two approaches. Heuristic warm-starting uses inexpensive approximate rewards during an initial phase before switching to refinement with exact rewards. Reward correction combines inexpensive estimates with randomized exact evaluations, preserving the expected policy gradient while reducing the expected number of exact solves per update. Experiments on three synthetic optimization problems demonstrate improvements over prediction-loss baselines, while a larger knapsack experiment shows faster early improvement under short training budgets. On inventory planning with H&M transactions and product descriptions, our best configuration, in which the LLM reasons before predicting, reduces regret by 31.4% relative to the SFT baseline and 12.4% relative to the strongest evaluated conventional forecasting baseline.

papers.title: Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity
papers.abstract: We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.

papers.title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference costs, the video and action experts can operate at different depths: visual features are computed once per query, whereas action computation repeats at every sampling step. We further propose elastic self-distillation, which trains a single elastic checkpoint, LoopedWAM-E, across action-depth and sampling-step budgets. With only 0.58B policy parameters and no robot pretraining, LoopedWAM achieves 96.1% success on LIBERO, 91.9% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 52.2% on RoboCasaGR1, while using $7.4\times$ less peak GPU memory than Fast-WAM under matched inference measurements. On LIBERO, LoopedWAM-E achieves 96.0% success in 27.6 ms or 95.2% in 24.7 ms on an H100, providing multiple accuracy-latency operating points from a single checkpoint; with two sampling steps and four action loops, it stays within 0.5 points of LoopedWAM on all three benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, LoopedWAM succeeds in 71.3% of 80 trials across four tasks.

papers.title: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models
papers.abstract: Comparative feedback, in which a judge says which of two candidate outcomes is closer to what happened, is a practical way to train language world models that assign probabilities to an action's outcomes. We show that, fitted with a Bradley-Terry objective, it need not teach the true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones. On a simulated robot push with enumerated outcome distributions, this objective takes a model that is accurate on unseen layouts (hazard error 2.4 percentage points, pp) and moves 33 to 43 pp of its probability onto outcomes that none of a condition's enumerated branches produces. The cause is the objective, not the comparisons: its optimum, computed before training, predicts where the model ends up, and a likelihood that knows the judge's rule learns from the same comparisons without the shift. The shift is robust: it recurs on unseen conditions, under five candidate laws and a three-fold denser enumeration, and about 29 pp remain without the physically impossible events. Its cost is conditional: with those events it inflates hazard probabilities, and a threshold inherited from the pre-feedback model costs about 3 pp of utility per decision on trained and 1 to 2 pp on unseen conditions, through false rejects; without them the utility loss averages below 1 pp over six seeds, though a small regret in action choice remains. Audits of readout, response and decision trace the effect from probabilities to actions.

papers.title: Characterizing Age-Conditioned Affective Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: An age prompt can change how a vision-language model (VLM) rates the emotion evoked by an image. Does the change predict how people of different ages rate that same image? We evaluate 17 VLMs on 900 OASIS images using young-, middle-, and older-adult prompts and estimate image-specific age differences from ratings by 822 participants. Without an age cue, models closely track average human valence (median Pearson $r=0.891$). Under an older-adult prompt, 16 of 17 models assign lower valence on average than under a young-adult prompt. Yet after adjusting for image pleasantness, correlations between model and human age effects range from $-0.030$ to $0.093$, against an estimated ceiling of $0.595$. The discrepancy is clearest on 54 sensitive images rated as pleasant. Across models, the older prompt reduces valence by $0.845$ points on average, while older participants rate these images $0.443$ points higher than younger participants. Providing human ratings from other images improves agreement on the direction of age differences, although image-specific fidelity remains modest on 600 held-out images ($r_{\mathrm{part}}=0.105$). These results show why evaluations of demographic personalization in foundation models need human comparisons at the level of individual stimuli. Project page available at https://shahriyar-zaman.github.io/age-conditioned-emotion-reasoning/

papers.title: From Data Alignment to Parameter Generation: Few-Shot Cross-City Traffic Prediction with Conditional Diffusion
papers.abstract: Accurate mobile traffic forecasting is crucial for network service management, supporting proactive capacity provisioning, congestion mitigation, and energy-efficient operation. However, many cities and regions are data-scarce (e.g., newly deployed or poorly instrumented areas), thus making traffic prediction a few-shot learning problem and limiting the practicality of standard data-driven models. Existing cross-city solutions primarily rely on data-space alignment to match traffic distributions between data-rich and data-scarce cities, but such alignment is often brittle under real-world distribution shifts, measurement noise, and city-specific bias. To address these limitations, we propose a Conditional Diffusion-based Parameter Generation (CDPG) framework. Instead of aligning raw data, CDPG learns the conditional distribution of high-performing predictor parameters for source cities and directly generates node-specific model parameters for the target city. To support reliable adaptation for network traffic prediction, CDPG conditions parameter generation on multi-modal spatio-temporal context. Specifically, CDPG captures spatial environment cues by combining satellite imagery with large language model (LLM)-derived semantic descriptions, and summarizes complex temporal behaviors via unsupervised pattern clustering. These contextual components guide CDPG in producing parameters tailored to each base station's operational context, thereby improving robustness under cross-city and cross-region shifts. Extensive experiments on three large-scale datasets show that CDPG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art cross-city few-shot baselines by up to 9.72% on standard forecasting metrics and remains robust for few-shot multi-step prediction. The code is available at https://github.com/LingoodBoy/CDPG.

papers.title: A full-color four-point form factor
papers.abstract: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

papers.title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tasks, such as summarization and question answering. However, they may produce hallucinations, false or misleading content not grounded in the source text, which can mislead analysts and corrupt downstream security decisions. This paper presents an exploratory measurement study of hallucinations in LLM-based CTI. We introduce HalluVision, a reproducible framework that generates LLM outputs, extracts domain-specific entities using a fine-tuned named entity recognition model, and evaluates factual consistency using multiple similarity metrics. Using 4,940 real-world cybersecurity articles, we measure hallucinations in outputs from two commercial LLMs and one open-weight LLM. Measurements are validated against 100 human-annotated outputs and two established faithfulness detectors. Results show that semantic similarity aligns with human judgments, whereas entity-based metrics exhibit limited agreement. Differences between models are concentrated in question answering, while entity extraction quality limits what entity-level metrics can reveal.

papers.title: GraF-VTA: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Vision and Temporal Logic via Graph-Based Fusion
papers.abstract: Robotic planning from visual observations and signal temporal logic (STL) requires grounding task requirements in scene evidence while adapting plans to execution feedback. We present GraF-VTA, a graph-based framework that extends Vision-TL-Action with structured task representations, causal observation history, and closed-loop trajectory generation. Bidirectional cross-attention fuses STL syntax tokens with visual features, while an optional frozen automaton embedding supplies complementary untimed task structure. A temporal pyramid preserves detailed current observations and compresses older frames to provide recent execution context. Conditioned on these features and robot state, a flow-matching model generates plans whose action prefixes are executed before replanning from refreshed observations. Across five simulation environments, the single-graph configuration achieves higher open-loop Success@$K$ than TeLoGraF and Vision-TL-Action on four environments at the reported budgets $K\geq16$. On Panda, matched-update ablations increase Success@256 from 53.91\% without observation history to 62.50\% with pyramid memory. In closed-loop Dubins evaluation, it reaches 64.06\% Success@1024, compared with 12.50\% for adapted S-MSP and 27.34\% for adapted Logic-VLA. These results support combining structured visual conditioning with observation history and replanning to improve coverage of STL-satisfying trajectories.

papers.title: Rubric Semantics or Numerical Priors? Auditing Scale-Direction Bias in LLM Judges
papers.abstract: Recent benchmark evaluations increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) as automatic judges. This paradigm assumes LLMs evaluate based on the rubric's semantic meaning rather than its numeric scale. We question this assumption by introducing semantic faithfulness: the principle that semantically equivalent rubrics must yield consistent scores. To quantify this, we propose a scale-reversal probe that inverts score anchors without altering evaluation criteria. Furthermore, we introduce floor normalization to calibrate reversal disagreement against intrinsic model variability, enabling fair cross-model comparisons. Experiments across five meta-evaluation benchmarks with seven diverse LLM judges spanning open-weight and proprietary models reveal widespread violations of semantic faithfulness, showing that raw reversal agreement alone is misleading. Finally, we demonstrate that bidirectional anchor averaging reduces dependence on any single anchor direction without compromising alignment with human judgments. Our findings emphasize that trustworthy LLM judges must reliably follow rubric semantics, not just correlate with human ratings.

papers.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
papers.abstract: Multimodal foundation models are advancing embodied navigation, but frequent inference incurs substantial computational cost. We present Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy. Retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback determine the cognitive horizon, or how many cached waypoints the robot executes before refreshing its prediction. At the policy's stop request, local visitation history guides a bounded correction with at most one extra movement and no additional model calls. CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% on HM3D-OVON and 64.7% on R2R-CE, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, respectively. Success rate and success weighted by path length improve per model call on both benchmarks. Across four physical navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 successes versus 14 for native execution, reducing model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%.

papers.title: Learning Networked Dynamical Systems via Neural ODE-based Graph Structure Inference
papers.abstract: Inferring the latent interaction graph from multivariate time series is fundamental to understanding complex dynamical systems in neuroscience, biology, and physics. Despite recent progress in neural relational inference, most methods rely on discrete-time modeling, which degrades under sparse and irregular observations and tends to entangle multi-hop dependencies into spurious direct edges. We show that a continuous-time formulation naturally decouples inference from any fixed observation schedule, allowing gradient signals to be integrated continuously between observations for both dynamics and structure learning. We propose NOGI (Neural ODE-based Graph Inference), a framework that couples a deterministic graph learner with an MPNN-based Neural ODE. The two modules are trained end-to-end via the adjoint method. Across four simulated dynamical systems at two scales, NOGI achieves the best structure recovery in 30 out of 32 evaluated cases with highly competitive forecasting performance, remaining robust under observation degradation. On the realistic Netsim fMRI benchmark, it attains an average AUPRC of 0.90 (AUROC 0.96). These results suggest that explicitly decoupling relational interactions from self-dynamics within a continuous-time vector field provides a powerful mechanism for graph structure learning under realistic observation conditions.

papers.title: AI-Driven Transformation of Digital Platform Work: A Task-Based Model for Measuring Labour Disruption and Vulnerability, with Early Evidence from Online Freelancing in Kenya
papers.abstract: Assessments of AI's impact on labour often rely on conventional occupational categories or broad market indicators. This dominant trend, however, obscures how tasks within the same occupation vary in practice across work arrangements. This limitation is particularly important in online freelancing, where workers are typically remote and devote substantial time performing unpaid tasks. This article introduces a task-based framework that distinguishes AI-driven disruption, defined as the extent of change in how work is performed, from livelihood vulnerability associated with that change. The framework is subsequently applied to assess the potential for automation, substitution, and enhancement across four categories of platform work: writing, virtual assistance, transcription, and web and software development. The model estimates high disruption across all four categories, while livelihood vulnerability scores are lower and vary by occupation. Potential efficiency gains on unpaid tasks partly offset potential wage impact associated with paid work in the model. The article compares these estimates with evidence from a survey of 52 online freelancers and 20 follow-up interviews in Nairobi, Kenya. Workers report changes in how they perform tasks and intensifying competition, while their accounts show how adapting their skills and using AI strategically shape their concerns about job loss. The findings show how task-based modelling can provide a baseline for assessing AI-driven changes in platform work and how workers' experiences differ from projections and help explain how these changes may threaten their livelihoods.

papers.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
papers.abstract: Background: Precision oncology requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and pathology data, yet many fusion models offer limited biologically grounded interpretability and struggle with missing modalities. Methods: We present Hierarchical Interpretable Tensor Fusion (HIT-Fuse), integrating six modalities: somatic copy number variation, DNA methylation, RNA sequencing, microRNA expression, RPPA protein abundance, and vision transformer-derived pathomics across four TCGA cohorts (glioma, lung adenocarcinoma, breast, and kidney cancer). Modality-specific autoencoders compress high-dimensional inputs, followed by two-stage CP tensor decomposition. Missing latent modalities are reconstructed using clinical covariates and observed omics to expand cohorts and retrain downstream models. A mathematical traceback mechanism enables global and local xAI attributions. Results: HIT-Fuse identifies distinct latent subgroups with significant survival stratification in glioma, breast, and kidney cohorts, both with complete and reconstructed modalities. Cohort expansion yields cohort-specific gains, including a 56.4% relative increase in weighted F1 for glioma. Biological validation against DepMap CRISPR screens, miRTarBase and RPPA annotations supports decoded drivers across all four cohorts. Essential gene rates range from 6.2% in glioma to 7.6% in lung cancer; example drivers include ANAPC11, SNRPD1, PLK1 and RPL14. Of decoded miRNAs, 71-92% have miRTarBase regulatory support, while 77-84% of selected genes are covered in DepMap. Conclusions: HIT-Fuse combines hierarchical tensor fusion, missing-modality reconstruction and traceable attributions to support interpretable multi-omics and digital pathology-based cancer prognosis across heterogeneous cohorts.

papers.title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on persistent memory to plan tool calls and complete multi-step tasks, which exposes them to memory drift: an adversarial or misleading memory alters the execution path and final outcome. In this work, we investigate online memory-drift detection, which estimates each retrieved memory's causal contribution to potential drift at serving time. We identify two fundamental challenges. (1) Content-level features are insufficient for causal memory-drift attribution, as perplexity or retrieval relevance alone cannot determine which retrieved memory would change agent behavior if neutralized; (2) Counterfactual attribution is prohibitively expensive for online detection, as it requires replaying downstream agent and tool execution for each candidate memory, exceeding real-time serving budgets. To address these challenges, we propose DriftGuard, a two-stage framework that decouples offline causal supervision from online estimation. Specifically, DriftGuard first constructs causal supervision through repeated paired counterfactual replays, continuing the original and single-memory neutralized trajectory suffixes from a shared pre-action state. The resulting annotations are aggregated by component-wise majority voting into a memory drift score (MDS) that captures action change, attack removal, violation removal, and task recovery. Guided by this supervision, DriftGuard then learns an online risk model that estimates MDS from pre-action information and flags drift-inducing memories via its maximum component risk, without online counterfactual rollouts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DriftGuard accurately identifies drift-inducing memories and enables efficient online defense. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DriftGuard-7F0B.

papers.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a well-established paradigm for augmenting large language models (LLMs) with information retrieved from external corpora. However, developing effective RAG systems requires substantial engineering effort and iterative experimentation, as effective design choices vary across tasks and domains. With rapid advances in LLM agent capabilities, we ask how well these agents can autonomously build RAG systems and how effectively they can improve them through iteration. In this paper, we propose AutoRAGBench, the first benchmark to evaluate how well LLM agents develop RAG systems from scratch in an open code space. It comprises nine RAG system development tasks. For each task, agents build RAG systems from scratch without starter code or prescribed strategies, under a six-hour budget on a single H800 GPU. They analyze task data, implement RAG pipelines, and iteratively refine their designs based on experimental feedback. We evaluate nine agent configurations and analyze both the effectiveness of the resulting RAG systems and their development trajectories. GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex CLI achieves the highest average score of 56.1. The composite Human-SOTA baseline averages 44.4. These results show that LLM agents can automate effective RAG system development. When starting from a human-designed system on each of seven tasks, GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex CLI improves the score by 16.6 points on average.

papers.title: A New Gravitational Wave Power Law from Dissipative Sound Waves in Cosmological Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Power-law behavior in cosmological gravitational wave (GW) spectra reveals the physical nature of their sources. For sound waves generated by cosmological first-order phase transitions, we identify a new high-frequency power law arising from the dissipative evolution of the acoustic source. In a dissipative plasma, the GW spectrum acquires an additional $q^{-2}$ suppression relative to the perfect-fluid result in the late-time, strong-damping limit. The exponent is largely insensitive to the source profile, while the turnover and suppression strength probe plasma transport and the source lifetime. In particular, the turnover frequency in weakly coupled hidden sector plasmas is sensitive to the underlying gauge coupling and can lie in the millihertz band targeted by space-based interferometers, opening a way to probe microscopic plasma dynamics through the detailed GW spectrum.

papers.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
papers.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems. We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.

papers.title: Syndrome-based Calibration Using Gate-Error Amplification
papers.abstract: We present Gate-Error Amplification for Recalibration with Syndromes (GEARS), a runtime calibration framework that uses gate-error amplification to efficiently tune control parameters during quantum error correction. Maintaining reliable control of large qubit arrays throughout hours-long computations requires repeated calibration to compensate for hardware drift. In conventional calibration, targeted qubits are temporarily removed from the code, introducing non-negligible space-time overhead. An elegant alternative uses syndrome information already collected during error correction as feedback for in situ recalibration, but acquiring signal requires sufficient (1) measurement budget or (2) probe strength, i.e., the size of deliberate control perturbations. More measurements improve statistical precision but result in slower control updates, while stronger perturbations produce larger calibration signals at the cost of additional errors. GEARS augments syndrome-based calibration with an established gate characterization technique called gate-error amplification. Our approach repeats selected CZ gates and probes their controls in spatially separated groups, strengthening local calibration signals while limiting the logical cost of probing. Surface code simulations show that GEARS with depth-three amplification reduces measurement requirements by approximately a factor of eight at matched gradient SNR and fixed probe strength. In closed-loop calibration, GEARS with depth-three amplification reduces excess expected logical failures by approximately 31-40% relative to calibration without amplification across the evaluated execution windows. Under time-dependent drift, GEARS increases the estimated critical drift frequency by approximately 1.9x. These results indicate that deliberately amplifying gate errors during operation can improve the long-time performance of quantum computations.

papers.title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical learning architectures provide a promising framework for integrating quantum feature transformations into complex data-processing tasks. Among these transformations, the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) offers a structured approach to feature processing, motivating an investigation of how its circuit configuration influences predictive performance, quantum resource requirements, and noise robustness. We present a hybrid PointNet-quantum neural network architecture for LiDAR point-cloud classification, combining classical feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit. Five Fourier-processing configurations are systematically evaluated: No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT. Experiments on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet across three random seeds assess classification performance, class-level behavior, circuit complexity, and sensitivity to the IBM FakeManilaV2 noise model. Under ideal simulation, IQFT-After achieves the highest weighted F1-score on KITTI (0.857 $\pm$ 0.033), compared with 0.838 $\pm$ 0.023 for No-QFT. Removing the final SWAP gates in the QFT circuit reduces circuit complexity while preserving the Pauli-Z measurement features up to a fixed permutation that can be absorbed by the classification head. Under quantum noise, the circuit ranking changes, with IQFT-After exhibiting greater performance degradation and No-QFT and Trainable-QFT showing stronger robustness. Per-class analysis further identifies dataset-dependent differences in minority-class performance. These results demonstrate that Fourier-processing configuration influences both classification behavior and noise sensitivity, highlighting the role of circuit structure and hardware-aware evaluation in hybrid quantum learning for three-dimensional point-cloud data.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing
papers.abstract: Objective: Case investigation and contact tracing are labor-intensive. Web forms struggle when respondents need clarification before disclosing contacts, and open-ended chatbots may deviate from protocols. We developed and evaluated Epira, a protocol-controlled large language model (LLM) interviewer for multi-disease case investigation and contact tracing. Materials and Methods: Epira pairs LLM dialogue with a rule-based controller enforcing required questions, safety handoffs, and a structured case record, and adapts to new diseases by questionnaire upload. Local (Qwen2.5) and cloud (GPT-5.4) backends were tested. Study 1 used 108 simulated cases with ground-truth fields and contacts for measles and gonorrhea under Epira and open-ended conditions (864 sessions). Study 2 enrolled 72 volunteers in a 2$\times$2 disease-by-model interview assessing completion, usability, acceptability, and trust. Results: Across Study 1, Epira with a local LLM captured 88.9% of required fields and 60.1% of ground-truth contacts. Open-ended interviewers recovered 31.1-41.9 percentage points fewer required fields than the same models in Epira. In Study 2, completion was 100%; mean adapted System Usability Scale (SUS) was 82.95 $\pm$ 16.17 on a 0-100 scale and mean trust was 3.85 $\pm$ 0.77 on a 1-5 scale. Discussion: Protocol control drove completeness more than model choice. Local and cloud deployments produced similar records, supporting privacy-preserving local use with human review of routed interviews and missed contacts. Conclusion: Epira recovers required fields and contacts under diverse disclosure conditions, works with local and cloud LLMs, and received favorable usability and trust ratings.

papers.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
papers.abstract: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

papers.title: Trajectory-Calibrated Merging of Embodied Policies
papers.abstract: Robot foundation models are increasingly adapted into task specialists to expand their embodied capabilities. Yet these capabilities remain fragmented across separate policies, and existing model-merging methods do not reliably preserve them during closed-loop execution: parameter-space alignment provides only an indirect proxy for behavior, while regression may fail to preserve behavior at states not covered by its calibration inputs. We present Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR), an execution-aware, gradient-free framework that consolidates robot specialists into a single policy. Across two complementary timescales, TCR collects calibration inputs from expert rollouts spanning different stages of task execution and from intermediate states within iterative action generation. To account for representation shifts introduced by merging, TCR recomputes each block's input through the already merged blocks. It then uses each expert's computation within the block to form module inputs and fits merged weights to match the experts' linear outputs. A two-pass calibration procedure further refines the merged policy using separate rollout caches while retaining the frozen specialists as teachers. The resulting model preserves the original inference graph and requires neither expert routing nor additional gradient training. On LIBERO, TCR merges four $π_{0.5}$ specialists and achieves 77.83% success across 1,200 evaluation episodes, outperforming FeatCal, RegMean, and direct weight averaging by 9.50, 24.17, and 33.00 percentage points, respectively.

papers.title: VidToC: Rethinking Video Token Compression for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Extending multimodal large language models (MLLMs) from images to videos faces substantial memory and latency challenges due to the massive number of visual tokens. These challenges have driven the development of numerous visual token compression methods and more efficient LLM architectures. However, existing compression methods are often evaluated with different training setups, tasks, and models, making fair comparison difficult. Meanwhile, the growing use of hybrid Mamba-Transformer architectures raises questions about whether compression strategies transfer across backbones. We present VidToC, a controlled evaluation framework for representative compression algorithms, LLM backbones, and time encoding strategies, covering training-free and fine-tuned settings on three complementary video understanding tasks. Our results reveal task-dependent compression behavior and characterize the effects of compression placement, time encoding, and backbone choice. These findings provide empirical guidance for designing and selecting video token compression strategies across tasks and training settings.

papers.title: Structure and Binding of the \texorpdfstring{$pnΩ^-$}{pnOmega} System with a Near-Unitary \texorpdfstring{$NΩ$}{NOmega} Interaction from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: The binding and spatial structure of the \(pnΩ^-\) system are investigated in the \(I(J^P)=0(5/2^+)\) channel using the physical-point HAL QCD \(NΩ({}^{5}S_2)\) interaction. The pairwise Hamiltonian includes the spin-triplet \(pn\) interaction and the finite-size Coulomb attraction in the \(pΩ^-\) pair. The three-body Schrödinger equation is solved with the Gaussian Expansion Method (GEM), including all three Jacobi rearrangement configurations. For the central HAL QCD potential at \(t/a=14\), the calculated three-body binding energy is \(18.63\) MeV, corresponding to a separation energy of \(16.39\) MeV relative to the \(d+Ω^-\) threshold. The spatial structure is examined through interparticle root-mean-square distances, pair and spectator radial distributions, and the correlation between the two Jacobi coordinates. Relative to a frozen-deuteron folded reference, the full three-body solution exhibits a substantially more compact spectator distribution and a contracted \(pn\) pair. The dependence on the Euclidean-time choice of the HAL QCD potential is also assessed. The results characterize the three-body rearrangement induced by the attractive \(NΩ\) interaction within the adopted pairwise model.

papers.title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified framework for sensing time-dependent fields through the lens of classical and quantum algorithms. First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks. These protocols attain the optimal sensitivity for linear and nonlinear AC sensing on conventional spin or qubit platforms, improving existing devices by changing only their pulse sequences. We then introduce quantum computational spectroscopy (QCS), which couples quantum sensors to a quantum processor. QCS combines two new primitives: a quantum computational frequency comb that coherently converts any classical signal into a quantum oracle, and a family of quantum algorithms that use the oracle to extract signal information in superposition. Variations can be implemented on current platforms with only one memory ancilla. We show that the ultimate limit imposed by quantum mechanics lies polynomially beyond the Heisenberg limit, and that QCS achieves it. Attaining this new limit requires quantum computation, establishing a fundamental separation between conventional and quantum computational sensing. Moreover, QCS retains beyond-Heisenberg scaling for broadband signals under constant-strength sensor depolarization, while we prove that the same noise limits any protocol lacking quantum computation to standard-quantum-limit scaling. Our result provides the first asymptotic, beyond-quadratic quantum advantage in AC metrology when noise is aligned with the signal, proving that Lindblad span conditions do not apply to broadband quantum sensing. Our work builds an algorithmic theory for designing sensing protocols and establishes quantum sensing as a new frontier for quantum algorithms, with quantum advantages that surpass the Heisenberg limit and that persist under noise.

papers.title: How zonal states beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes stabilize micro-turbulence in tokamak plasmas
papers.abstract: The effects of zonal states (ZS) beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes (AEs) on micro-turbulence stability are investigated; taking toroidal Alfven eigenmode (TAE) and ion temperature gradient mode (ITG) as an example. The analysis is carried out by deriving the nonlinear gyrokinetic equation describing particle response to ITG, in the presence of TAE beat-driven ZS. It is found that, the phase space zonal structure generated by AEs could lead to a significant reduction in the local nonuniformity drive and, thereby, stabilize the local ITG instabilities. The zonal flow induced shearing, on the other hand, contributes only to a real frequency shift and, typically, negligibly small additional stabilization.

papers.title: Reinforcement-Aligned Probabilistic Weather Forecasting with Discrete Tokens
papers.abstract: Global medium-range weather forecasting must not only generate ensembles efficiently to characterize uncertainty in future states, but also serve downstream applications such as extreme-event warnings and cross-sphere coupled simulations. We introduce WeatherCraft, a framework that unifies probabilistic generation and reinforcement learning alignment through discrete weather tokens, bringing the GPT-style pretraining--post-training paradigm to global medium-range weather forecasting. A multiscale tokenizer represents atmospheric states as a coarse-to-fine token hierarchy, while a Transformer models causal dependencies across time and scale and predicts tokens within each scale in parallel. Direct sampling generates diverse ensembles, and exact token log-probabilities enable Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to maximize downstream task rewards without differentiating through evaluators or coupled models. On the ERA5 benchmark, WeatherCraft's eight-member ensemble mean reduces day-15 normalized RMSE by 17.6% relative to the strongest evaluated deterministic baseline and, with KV caching, achieves an approximately $18\times$ inference speedup over GenCast. Direct fair-CRPS adaptation improves ensemble probabilistic skill, while reward-based post-training improves forecasts of persistent land temperature extremes and coupled ocean heat extremes. This work establishes discrete autoregressive modeling as a general foundation for scalable, task-alignable Earth system foundation models.

papers.title: UMelCodec: An Ultra-Low-Bitrate and Lightweight Mel-Domain Neural Speech Codec
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-bitrate speech coding is crucial for bandwidth-constrained communication and compact storage, but preserving intelligibility, naturalness, and fine-grained acoustic details at bitrates of only a few hundred bps remains challenging. Existing purely acoustic codecs generally operate at relatively high bitrates, whereas incorporating semantic representations can reduce the bitrate, but at the cost of increased complexity. Therefore, we propose UMelCodec, a purely acoustic neural speech codec operating in the mel domain at an ultra-low bitrate of 325 bps with a lightweight architecture. UMelCodec consists of two stages. In the first mel-domain coding stage, alias-free Snake-ConvNeXt (AF-SC) encoder-decoder backbones model temporal and harmonic structures, a factorized single-codebook vector quantizer (VQ) enables ultra-low-bitrate quantization, and a multi-scale mel-spectrogram discriminator (MSMD) improves mel-spectrogram reconstruction. In the second waveform synthesis stage, a lightweight modified discrete cosine transform (MDCT)-based neural vocoder predicts the MDCT spectrum from the reconstructed mel spectrogram and recovers the waveform through inverse MDCT. Experiments on LibriTTS dataset demonstrate that UMelCodec outperforms strong baselines across most objective reconstruction metrics while maintaining competitive subjective naturalness. In terms of model complexity and inference efficiency, UMelCodec has only 19.67 M parameters, requires 1.93 G MACs, and supports real-time inference on both GPU and CPU platforms.

papers.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing
papers.abstract: Aerial sensing must combine uncertain overhead context with current observations while budgeting prediction, movement and image processing. AeroBelief uses the next executable action as the unit of verification against reference scores. It groups candidate views by first action, scans them with an inexpensive proposer, and selectively queries a structured world model (WM). Calibrated group bounds support strict commitment; a six-query controller connects selective prediction with belief updates, acceptance checks and scheduled sensing. Across four layout families, 40 worlds and 960 closed-loop executions, the AeroBelief controller completes 75.42% of tasks, compared with 73.33% for exhaustive WM scoring and 65.83% for line-of-sight geometry, using 91.81% fewer reference-candidate evaluations than exhaustive scoring. In fixed-reference replay with a six-query cap, proposer-scaled anchored bounds raised first-action certificate availability from 36.25% to 54.69% and reduced mean queries per state by 13.54% relative to unit-scale anchored bounds. A complete ground-hosted pipeline processes 2,685 self-collected 20-megapixel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images from seven DJI Mavic 3M routes. Context-guided admission and feedback retain all eight independently supported target confirmations with 76.05% fewer processed images and 70.02% less accumulated active processing service than uncapped all-frame processing; feedback saves another 5.17% of images relative to static context. The studies connect budgeted action selection with evidence-driven processing of recorded flight imagery.

papers.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
papers.abstract: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the video ends. We compare a modular pipeline, with separate step identification, temporal localization, and execution verification, to a joint model that predicts all outputs in a single step. To support supervised learning from mistakes, we repartition EgoPER to include erroneous videos in all splits. The approaches achieve similar step-segmentation F1@0.5 (93.6% and 92.1%), while the joint model achieves higher binary mistake-detection F1@0.5 (84.1% vs. 80.7%), with its largest gain on slips (56.4% vs. 37.5%). Component-level analysis suggests that error propagation between stages contributes to the modular approach's lower detection score. On test videos containing mistakes, both designs outperform released AEM and ESTANet checkpoints under our evaluation protocol.

papers.title: Diagnosis is not a policy: a state-transition audit of caoability-conditioned test-time inference
papers.abstract: Test-time actions can satisfy retrieval, state-realization, program-consistency, or rendering objectives without correcting an answer. Test-time Error Response and Realizability Audit (TERRA) is an evaluation/auditing protocol, not a new inference algorithm. It uses a unified decomposition of intervention outcomes into applicability, target-state realization, endpoint translation, harm, and resource/inference cost. Paired comparisons fix the incoming state and evaluation conditions; cross-model analyses vary the receiving configuration. Executable financial reasoning experiments yield three findings: the same context expansion can harm one configuration and benefit another; sufficient evidence does not ensure correctness because configurations differ in evidence-to-answer translation; and diagnostic headroom---accuracy attainable with idealized diagnostic information over the measured baseline---plus local consistency does not ensure practical gains. Action value is $V(a\mid x,m)$, not diagnosis alone; diagnosis is not a deployable policy $π(a\mid x,m)$.

papers.title: A Heterogeneous CPU-GPU Framework for Finite Element Micromagnetic Simulations on Tetrahedral Meshes
papers.abstract: The design of magnetic storage materials relies on repeated micromagnetic simulations. Within each simulation, the demagnetization field evaluation and the sparse linear solve are executed at every time step and together dominate the computational cost. To address these bottlenecks, we develop a heterogeneous CPU-GPU framework that exploits the complementary computational capabilities of the two processors. In the existing AFEMAG solver, developed by Yang et al [J. Comput. Phys. 431 (2021) 110142], computationally intensive boundary integral evaluations and sparse linear solves limit performance. We offload these operations to the GPU while retaining assembly and iteration control on the CPU. We validate the framework using cases from all five $μ$Mag standard problems, covering quasistatic hysteresis, equilibrium configurations, field-driven dynamics, and spin-transfer-torque dynamics. This approach accelerates simulations across the benchmark suite; notably, for Standard Problem 3 on a mesh of 137,313 nodes, augmenting the CPU with one NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a $17.1\times$ speedup over the CPU-only configuration. The heterogeneous AFEMAG framework thus provides an efficient and practical platform for micromagnetic simulations in the design of magnetic storage materials.

papers.title: Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary of $C^{1, η}$ open sets
papers.abstract: We study the boundary behavior of nonnegative harmonic functions for a class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes in $C^{1,η}$ open sets $D\subset\mathbb R^d$. The jump kernels are allowed to blow up at the boundary of $D$ and the processes may have a critical killing potential. We identify the exact boundary decay exponent $p$, characterized by the coefficient of the critical killing potential. We establish a boundary Harnack principle which yields the comparability of $f(x)/δ_D(x)^p$ for nonnegative harmonic functions that vanish continuously on a portion of the boundary. The key ingredient of the proof combines estimates of the exact decay rate for the survival probability of the killed process with a modified box method and uses a regularized distance function to handle the limited boundary regularity.

papers.title: Geometry-induced orientational trapping dictates escape of active rods in corrugated channels
papers.abstract: The non-equilibrium transport of anisotropic active matter through geometrically confined environments is fundamentally governed by the interplay between self-propulsion and geometry-induced entropic barriers. Using overdamped Langevin dynamics, we reveal contrasting escape mechanisms of self-driven rods in narrow corrugated channels by comparing smoothly varying sinusoidal (SC) geometries to circular (CC) cavities with localized, uniform curvature. We observe a strictly non-monotonic dependence of the mean first escape time (MFET) with increasing Peclet number (Pe) in the CC channel, contrary to the monotonic dependence in the SC channel. This non-monotonicity emerges from a competition between activity-enhanced escape at low-to-intermediate propulsion and persistent, geometry-induced orientational trapping along the circular boundary at high propulsion, which inhibits reorientation toward the exit neck. This regime crossover is further corroborated by trajectory-to-trajectory escape fluctuations and bimodal radial probability distributions reflecting persistent wall-collision and wall-aligned sliding transport. The self part of van-Hove correlation function exhibits distinct anisotropic non-Gaussian displacements in the SC channel, in contrast to symmetric profiles with extended active-trapping plateaus in the CC cavities. These results establish local channel topology as a critical determinant of confined active transport, with direct implications for microfluidic sorting, biological navigation, and targeted drug delivery in corrugated environments.

papers.title: AZOWL AgentOps: Task-Scoped Governance for Deployed Agent Applications
papers.abstract: AZOWL AgentOps provides shared governance for deploying agents and delegating work to them. Human and agent senders can exchange messages or explicitly delegate a business task. Accepted work has a stable identifier that links the sender's authority, the assigned runner, any required approval, and result evidence. The default enrolled customer PC profile is read-only. We compare AZOWL components with a configured LangGraph application in 28 synthetic runs across four paired pilots. Original AZOWL services checked work admission, recipient routing, and workflow prerequisites in isolated tests. The configured LangGraph application supplied business task and dispatch records in application code. Both configurations recorded zero business tasks in dialogue, rejected unauthorized agent handoffs, and issued zero writes when an approved delivery address changed. AZOWL's scope gate, exercised as a component, requested approval again on the same task. A product probe reused one registered provider across two workflows and checked prerequisite enforcement for ticket-task submission. The paired protected writes, including ticket creation, used mock providers. Of two deployed PC inventory reads with verified receipts, we traced the 0.6.57 run from submission through runner pickup and tool execution to the receipt, with matching local and central artifact hashes. A separate deployed GRC audit followed an operator-driven ticket lifecycle on sample records.

papers.title: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, a Detection Benchmark and an Audit of Published Image Ciphers
papers.abstract: NPCR, the share of ciphertext bytes changed by a one-pixel plaintext change, is reported for nearly every image cipher as evidence of diffusion, with 99.61% the target. Several mechanisms produce values near it, and the mean does not say which. We separate three regimes: no propagation, one round of forward and backward chaining linear over addition or XOR, and independent ciphertexts. For the second an exact count applies. After a least-significant-bit change its mean asymptotically matches the independent-ciphertext reference, while its spread without cancellation is about five to twenty times larger. In simulation, the one-sided NPCR test of Wu, Noonan and Agaian flags one-round additive, mixed and S-box chaining in 2-4% of papers; read in both directions, the same five values flag at least 99.9%. Two-sided testing does the detecting; the spread and the other signatures help diagnose the structure. We then audit twenty-one published schemes. The count matches a reimplementation of one published diffusion layer on every trial and accounts for its reported table, the signatures show two schemes whose printed specifications cannot produce their reported values, and find that three of our own report plain-versus-cipher values and fall to two chosen images; ten more change their encryption material with the plaintext or per encryption, so their NPCR mostly reflects that change. A released checker applies the signatures to published tables, showing what a table measures within stated assumptions; it does not certify security.

papers.title: Is a Description Worth a Thousand Demonstrations? Specificity and Reliability of Task Descriptions in In-Context Learning
papers.abstract: A prompt for in-context learning (ICL) can describe a task in addition to, or instead of, demonstrating it through examples. Yet how task descriptions work remains poorly understood theoretically. Through the Bayesian view of ICL, we model descriptions as informative priors characterized by their specificity and reliability. We adapt the effective sample size (ESS) from Bayesian statistics, quantifying a description's predictive value as an equivalent number of demonstrations. For in-context linear regression, we show that a reliable description's ESS grows with its specificity and with the task's dimension. A description that may be irrelevant, however, gains little from its specificity unless demonstrations are given. In practice, do in-context learners use descriptions as a Bayes-optimal predictor would? Our experiments show that meta-trained Transformers come close to the Bayes-optimal ESS when tested on their training distribution. Pretrained language models, however, make too little use of highly specific descriptions when answering without reasoning; most of them closely match the Bayes-optimal predictor only when reasoning is enabled. These results extend the Bayesian analysis of ICL from demonstrations to descriptions.

papers.title: k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
papers.abstract: The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetković in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$. For each fixed $k\geq2$, we also determine the $k$-trees attaining the largest second largest eigenvalue below $1$ and the smallest above $1$. Finally, we determine all minimal forbidden induced subgraphs among $k$-trees with $k\geq 1$, each of which has second largest eigenvalue greater than $1$, but deleting any vertex gives a graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$.

papers.title: Communication-Aware UAV Spatio-Temporal Relay Cooperation and Planning in Complex Urban Environments
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in low-altitude urban airspace for delivery, emergency response, and other applications. However, UAV mobility across spatially heterogeneous urban communication environments can lead to time-varying communication outages, disrupting mission execution and compromising flight safety. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Spatio-Temporal Relay Cooperation and Planning (ST-RCP) framework that leverages delivery UAVs as opportunistic communication relays for disconnected UAVs without requiring additional communication infrastructure. The framework predicts communication blind-spot events over a finite planning horizon, constructs a helper-event compatibility graph, and jointly optimizes relay selection, obstacle-aware trajectory replanning, and communication-aware scheduling. Multiple planners are evaluated to investigate the trade-offs among communication coverage, computational cost, and energy consumption. Experiments based on real-world traffic scenarios compare the performance of ST-RCP against baseline methods. In the peak scenario, ST-RCP improves descent-phase communication coverage by 29.93% compared with the base-station baseline and by 27.38%, 22.02%, and 15.20% compared with configurations using one, two, and three dedicated relay UAVs, respectively. Process flexibility analysis demonstrates that predictive task-aware relaying expands the pool of feasible relay resources and improves communication continuity while maintaining the feasibility of delivery missions. These findings demonstrate the potential of trajectory-enabled UAV coordination to enhance the safety and resilience of urban aerial operations.

papers.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction
papers.abstract: Task-specific rubrics are increasingly used to evaluate open-ended language-model outputs, yet constructing comprehensive evaluation criteria from complex source documents remains challenging. We study automatic rubric construction in professional mergers and acquisitions (M&A) due diligence, where evaluation criteria must be inferred from task instructions and supporting documents without access to an expert-authored reference rubric. We introduce a multi-axis generation framework that explores complementary structural and free-form views of the source evidence to construct a broad pool of candidate evaluation criteria. To distinguish failures of criterion discovery from failures of candidate selection, we introduce the coverage-selection gap, which measures the difference between reference-free ranking and a reference-informed greedy diagnostic under a fixed selection budget. Developed on 16 tasks and evaluated on four held-out tasks, our framework achieves 0.876 macro recall against senior-authored reference rubrics under an LLM-based criterion-equivalence protocol. Ablation studies further show that introducing new structural search axes improves recall by 6-10 percentage points, whereas increasing generation volume along existing search directions yields at most 1.5 points. These findings suggest that, once a high-coverage candidate pool has been constructed, effective reference-free selection becomes a substantial bottleneck in document-grounded rubric construction.

papers.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Agent Framework for CKM-Assisted Network Deployment Optimization
papers.abstract: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) offer reusable, site-specific radio priors to facilitate environment-aware network planning. However, deploying heterogeneous network nodes to meet diverse performance requirements in complex environments is challenging and requires executable workflows that coordinate scene preparation, candidate-site specification, CKM construction, optimization, and validation. This paper presents a large language model (LLM)-orchestrated agent framework for CKM-assisted network deployment optimization, where an LLM translates high-level requirements into modular, typed, and reproducible planning workflows. In this framework, an LLM layer interprets intent, selects modules, and populates normalized configurations; physics-grounded modules generate scene, CKM, optimization, and validation artifacts; and a deterministic guarded controller performs validation-guided refinement. A common target-candidate-CKM-optimizer interface supports the registration and composition of compatible planning modules, with CKM backends, samplers, and solvers remaining replaceable. We instantiate the proposed framework for base station (BS) deployment, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. An urban-block case study demonstrates automatic scene consistency checks, bounded BS/IRS deployment refinement, and collision- and radio-feasible UAV planning.

papers.title: UniReFP: Robust Unified Fingerprinting for Vision Models against Cross-Task Repurposing Attacks
papers.abstract: We identify, for the first time, a new model modification attack--the cross-task model repurposing attack--that can render fingerprints generated by existing model fingerprinting approaches inapplicable. To address this challenge, we propose UniReFP--a novel unified model fingerprinting framework applicable to diverse vision models across different tasks--that utilizes ownership evidence in a shared class-level semantic space rather than original task-specific output space, enabling effective ownership verification when a protected model is repurposed across tasks with heterogeneous output formats. Specifically, UniReFP constructs a surrogate classifier by repurposing the protected model, enabling fingerprints to be generated independently of the original task-dependent output space of the protected model. Moreover, it optimizes grouped fingerprints to encode ownership evidence: fingerprints within the same group are encouraged to induce consistent semantic responses and intermediate representations on the surrogate classifier, while producing dispersed responses on independently trained reference classifiers. During verification, UniReFP uses a task-aware semantic projection mechanism to map heterogeneous suspect-model outputs into unified semantic-presence vectors, and determines ownership by measuring inner-group consistency. Extensive experimental results validate the effectiveness of UniReFP, consistently showing superior performance under cross-task repurposing attacks, commonly studied model modification attacks, and even their combinations.

papers.title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
papers.abstract: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With μ* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.

papers.title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned video prediction lets robots anticipate the visual consequences of their actions for planning and policy evaluation. Existing predictors denoise each future from noise without using their own estimate of it, which limits the quality of the predicted future, in particular of the manipulated objects, and requires many network calls. We present TwoPass, a self-conditioned training-and-inference framework that keeps the standard flow-matching objective. Self-Generated Draft Training supplies a detached clean-video estimate from the shared network as conditioning at the same noisy state. A Refinement-Only Late Adapter applies a dedicated residual transformation when a draft is present. At inference, Draft-Reuse Iterative Refinement obtains both a solver update and the next draft from each velocity prediction, requiring as few as 4 function evaluations (NFE) per video chunk. Training samples discrete solver-query noise levels and updates the pretrained backbone. Extensive experiments on Bridge and Language Table show that TwoPass achieves state-of-the-art results with 4 NFE, far fewer than the 50-59 calls of existing predictors. Code: https://github.com/PlantPotatoOnMoon/TwoPass.

papers.title: Direct measurement of the on-shot focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class petawatt laser
papers.abstract: We report a direct, on-shot determination of the focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class, four-beam petawatt laser. Encircled-energy curves were inferred from the energy transmitted around aluminum-coated spheres of varying diameters placed at the focal plane. The 50% encircled-energy diameter D50 of each beam was obtained by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture with Bayesian inference. With all deformable mirrors optimized in closed loop, the best-corrected alignment beam reached D50 = 34 (+4/-5) um, three times the diffraction limit of 10 um. Under full-power conditions, the thermal distortion of the main amplifier broadened this beam to D50 = 102 (+9/-8) um and reduced its peak intensity ninefold, to 2.2 (+0.6/-0.9) x 10^18 W/cm^2 at 250 J and 1.3 ps. The energy fraction of the narrow component decreased from 68% to 38%. These reference values serve facility users, and a deformable mirror upstream of the pulse compressor, now on one beam only, doubles the on-shot peak intensity.

papers.title: Anchored Inertial Proposals with Objective Verification for Diffusion-Prior Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Training-free diffusion priors are powerful for inverse problems, but measurement guidance during reverse sampling is local: aggressive updates can improve immediate data fit while disrupting later denoising. We introduce an anchored inertial correction rule that separates proposal generation from acceptance. At each corrected step, the denoiser prediction anchors a frozen clean-space objective combining measurement fit with a noise-level-dependent proximal term. Heavy-ball dynamics with step size and momentum computed from the measured curvature generate a clean-state candidate; a separate verifier evaluates it with the same objective, with the denoiser prediction retained as fallback; both stages are derived from one objective for the whole trajectory, considered one step at a time. The accepted clean state is re-noised to continue sampling. The rule applies to pixel and latent diffusion with differentiable measurement operators, requires no retraining, and adds no denoiser calls inside the correction loop. We analyze how objective verification yields local nonincrease and displacement control. Across natural-image benchmarks, the method achieves competitive reconstruction quality. Code is available at https://github.com/Seunghyeok0715/PIVOT2026.

papers.title: Depth of Powers of Cover Ideals of Path Ideals
papers.abstract: Let $ J_t(P_n) = (x_1, \ldots, x_t) \cap \cdots \cap (x_{n-t+1}, \ldots, x_n) $ be the cover ideal of the $t$-path ideal of a path graph inside the polynomial ring $ S = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n] $ over a field $K$. For every $ n \ge t \ge 2 $ and $s \ge 2$, we prove that \[ \operatorname{depth} \left ( S/J_t(P_n)^s \right ) = q(s+1) + \left\lfloor \frac{r-1}{t} \right\rfloor, \] where $ n = q(ts + 1) + r $ with $ 1 \le r \le ts + 1 $. Our proof shows that all powers of $J_t(P_n)$ have linear quotients in increasing lexicographic order and explicitly describes the corresponding colon ideals.

papers.title: Adaptive Tests of Pricing Restrictions with Observed and Latent Factors
papers.abstract: This paper develops a high-dimensional test for asset pricing models with observed and latent factors. The null hypothesis allows the intercepts from an observed-factor regression to be nonzero, provided that they lie in the latent factor loading space. We estimate the pricing errors in three steps: regress returns on the observed factors, extract latent factors from the lagged covariance structure of the regression residuals, and regress returns on both observed and estimated latent factors. The intercept from the final regression serves as the estimated pricing error. We construct Sum and Max tests based on the estimated pricing errors to detect diffuse and concentrated alternatives, respectively, and combine them using a Cauchy procedure. Under suitable regularity conditions, we establish the joint null distribution of the component statistics, their asymptotic independence, and their power against alternative hypotheses. We also propose a residual bootstrap and establish its first-order validity. Simulation studies examine the finite-sample performance of the tests under different pricing-error patterns and factor-number choices. An application to S\&P 500 stocks illustrates the use of the proposed framework in evaluating an observed-factor pricing model after latent-factor adjustment.

papers.title: LBW-NPS: A Local Band-Weighted Noise Power Spectrum Loss for Texture-Preserving Low-Dose CT Denoising
papers.abstract: Low-dose CT denoising should suppress noise while retaining the local texture of the reference image. Matching a pooled spectrum can overlook regional discrepancies, whereas pixel losses alone can favor overly smooth outputs. We propose a local band-weighted noise power spectrum loss (LBW-NPS) that compares spectral energies within overlapping Hann-tapered patches, without tissue-specific loss conditioning. Each valid patch contributes a weighted squared log-energy difference across three frequency bands, alongside an $L_1$ reconstruction term. We compare LBW-NPS against $L_1$-only training and five auxiliary-loss baselines using the same U-Net and three seeds on DeepLesion slices with simulated low-dose acquisitions, including patch-scale ablations and lung, soft-tissue, and bone evaluations. On 220 test slices from 31 patients, LBW-NPS reduces a local spectral gap related to the loss, on $64\times64$-pixel evaluation windows, by 31.9% relative to pooled band-weighted NPS, without a statistically significant PSNR change. This improvement is supported by lower errors relative to the reference in average NPS frequency and gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) measures not used in the loss, evaluated in homogeneous soft tissue.
