Against a geometry-only conditioner with the same parameter count, trained at three matched seeds, it is higher by $+1.25\pm0.72$ NDS and $+0.87\pm0.21$ mAP, on mAP in every pair, and the control's mean NDS is near the baseline's. An exploratory far-range gain failed an internally pre-specified held-out test, and large inference-time substitution penalties also occur without query-local evidence: neither learned allocation nor inference-time dependence substitutes for matched end-to-end comparisons.

papers.title: The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.

papers.title: Reproducing $J/ψ\to γ+3P$ data with meson spectroscopy and understanding $X(2370)$
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/ψ$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/ψ\toγPPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0η^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $η(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $η_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/ψ\toγπ^0π^0η$ and $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

papers.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,μ\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop within $1\,μ\text{s}$ while sustaining QPU-rate throughput. By introducing QuFrameISA, we cleanly decouple instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management. Execution is distributed across per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines (IREs) that resolve instructions against the frame via a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit enables independent, lock-free concurrent commits. To strictly guarantee the $1\,μ\text{s}$ deadline, QuFrame pairs an asynchronous primary decoder with an on-chip fallback decoder that resolves in $144\,\text{ns}$, natively reconciling divergent updates in hardware without degrading logical error rates.

papers.title: LipSpell: A Language-Independent Phonetic Scoring Framework for Spelling Correction Combining Distinctive-Feature Edit Distance, Keyboard Geometry, and Corpus Frequency
papers.abstract: Automatic spelling correction must handle both keyboard typographical slips and cognitive or phonetic misspellings where writers approximate a word's pronunciation. Conventional spell checkers rely either on orthographic edit distance and keyboard proximity--which struggle when phonetic errors diverge by multiple characters--or on English-centric phonetic hashes such as Soundex and Metaphone. We present LipSpell, a unified, language-independent phonetic scoring engine paired with swappable language-specific G2P frontends, keyboard maps, and lexicons integrating: (1) a precomputed |P|x|P| phone-distance matrix from universal IPA distinctive features, (2) physical keyboard geometry, and (3) corpus unigram frequency priors, accelerated by a two-stage symmetric-delete and seven-class phonetic-code index. Across six English benchmarks (including 1,000 L2 errors from TOEFL-Spell), LipSpell outperforms Norvig and Hunspell on every dataset and beats Aspell on Norvig1 (78.52% vs. 75.56%), Holbrook (32.00% vs. 26.67%), and TOEFL-Spell (77.30% vs. 72.80%). Evaluated across six languages spanning five branches (Germanic, Romance, Slavic, Semitic, Turkic), three families (Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Turkic), and three scripts, LipSpell achieves strong fixed-weight transfer on Brazilian Portuguese (73.00% Top-1 on n=500 Wikipedia without NFD tolerance and 75.80% with NFD vs. 66.40% Norvig, 64.20% Hunspell, 64.00% Aspell) and Russian Cyrillic (85.67% vs. 78.50% Norvig). On 50/50 clean non-word splits with lexicon cleaning and weak-character indels, tuning yields strong gains over Norvig in Portuguese (86.97% vs. 76.75%), Turkish (81.67% vs. 79.05%), Hebrew Abjad (74.59% vs. 62.30%), and French (74.53% vs. 67.92%), while fixed weights remain optimal for English (80.37%) and Russian (85.67%).

papers.title: Look Closer, Look Back, or Wait for Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Streaming video models must answer questions about a live video under strict memory and latency limits. Feeding only the latest few frames keeps present perception sharp, whereas adding past frames dilutes attention on the current scene and triggers hallucinations. Recent cascade methods retrieve past frames when uncertain, but they still fail when current frames are blurry or when decisive future clues have not appeared yet. We introduce ActiveForager, a streaming video agent that maintains a clean short working window and gathers extra evidence only on demand. For each query, the agent either answers directly, zooms into high-resolution recent frames, recalls past events from memory, or waits for upcoming frames. When recalling history, a shared-weight sub-agent verifies candidate clips in isolation and returns a compact evidence summary. A stream-decoupled attention mask then keeps historical evidence from interfering with present visual tokens. We train this policy using counterfactual information gain, which rewards a tool call only when the gathered evidence makes the true answer more likely and prevents tool collapse across all actions. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B on OVO-Bench, ActiveForager improves real-time perception, historical recall, and proactive response at once, lifting overall accuracy on Qwen3-VL-8B from 47.6% to 65.9%. It also doubles zero-shot accuracy on the multi-hop Video-Holmes benchmark while adding minimal visual tokens per query.

papers.title: Do Thinking VLMs Need to Keep Looking at Long Videos? Write It Down, Then Look Away
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) reason about long videos over hundreds to thousands of tokens. Every decoding step re-reads the key-value (KV) cache of the entire video. Must the model keep looking while it reasons? In LookAway, the model first writes timestamped notes on what the question needs and then puts the video away. Once the notes close, the inference engine hides the video's KV cache for the rest of the response. Across both hybrid and pure-attention VLMs, dependence on the video is concentrated early in the response. On Qwen3.6-27B, writing notes preserves accuracy better than free reasoning at the same withdrawal step. Replacing them with another video's notes harms accuracy, whereas keeping the video visible alongside the model's own notes adds no significant benefit. Without additional training, LookAway nearly matches full-video thinking accuracy at 0.12-0.13 times its modeled decode cost. To shorten this initial look, we fine-tune the model on its own correct LookAway responses. Reinforcement learning then rewards correct answers while penalizing KV reads. The trained model puts the video away after a median of 66-68 tokens. Across three held-out benchmarks, it writes more tokens than an identically trained full-video model yet reads only 27-35% as many KV positions at matched accuracy.

papers.title: FedE2E: One-Shot Federated Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Closed-Loop Evaluation
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without sharing datasets. However, existing federated learning methods for autonomous driving typically require multi-round communication and lack closed-loop evaluation, while one-shot methods mainly focus on perception tasks. To address these limitations, we propose \method, a one-shot federated learning method for end-to-end autonomous driving. It comprises multi-client calibration, anchor-based feature alignment, and token-wise consensus distillation to distill knowledge from heterogeneous models. Closed-loop evaluation on Bench2Drive demonstrates the effectiveness of \method in both one-shot and multi-round federated learning. In the one-shot setting, it achieves a Driving Score of 55.85, which is 4.07 points higher than prior work. In the multi-round setting, it reaches 60.35 after five communication rounds, the best performance among all compared methods under the same number of communication rounds.

papers.title: A Tight Broad-line Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots and Its Consequence for Virial Black Hole Masses
papers.abstract: JWST has uncovered compact high-redshift sources with red, $\sim 5000$ K optical continua and broad Balmer lines, known as "little red dots" (LRDs). Whether these lines trace gas orbiting a massive black hole or electron scattering in a dense, Eddington-limited envelope around a lighter black hole leaves inferred masses spanning $10^{4}$-$10^{8}\,M_{\odot}$. We test both pictures by uniformly refitting public JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 29 LRDs, 15 other JWST broad-line sources, and luminosity-matched SDSS quasars. At fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity, LRD broad $\mathrm{H}α$ widths have an intrinsic scatter of 0.054 dex ($<0.075$ dex at 95%), less than half that of quasars (0.12 dex), clustering near $1760\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ outside the three brightest sources. Because single-epoch virial masses scale as width squared, they scatter intrinsically by $<0.16$ dex at fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity, making virial masses and mass functions nearly deterministic restatements of luminosity regardless of the underlying physics. Compared with the Keplerian speed $v_{\rm K}$ at the photosphere of an Eddington-limited envelope, from each source's measured continuum luminosity and temperature, observed widths are 2.5-3.0 $v_{\rm K}$ (2-3$\times$ standard expectations for virial factors $f_{\rm vir}\approx 0.5$-1), with a quarter of the flux above escape speed and no detected continuum-luminosity dependence at fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity. Bound orbits outside a spherical photosphere thus require sub-Eddington optical luminosities ($\leq 0.10$-0.30 $L_{\rm Edd}$, a requirement specific to spherical photospheres), whereas an Eddington or super-Eddington spherical envelope requires uniform 2-3$\times$ non-gravitational broadening within the $\mathrm{H}α$-emitting gas.

papers.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
papers.abstract: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

papers.title: GenRF: Generative Registration-free Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Multi-modal image fusion combines complementary observations to improve scene visibility and perception. However, in real-world acquisition, differences in sensing principles and configurations introduce geometric discrepancies, while degradations further compromise source quality. Existing methods typically rely on explicit registration, yet large parallax complicates correspondence estimation, while mismatched fields of view leave some regions without cross-modal counterparts. Meanwhile, independent restoration underuses cross-modal information, whereas restoration-fusion methods assuming alignment remain vulnerable to misregistration. This study revisits misaligned and degraded image fusion in the era of generative foundation models, in which cross-attention enables position-agnostic complementary information aggregation, while generative priors support degradation recovery and inference in missing regions. Building on this perspective, we propose GenRF, which adapts pretrained FLUX through LoRA to jointly enhance degraded observations, infer missing cross-modal context, and fuse complementary information without explicitly estimating deformation fields. Extensive experiments on real-world infrared and visible captures show that GenRF delivers high-quality fusion directly from unregistered, degraded images without preprocessing, while improving downstream task performance under misalignment. Additional experiments demonstrate that GenRF can generalize to misaligned multi-exposure and multi-focus image fusion without task-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot
papers.abstract: Embodied models depend on real interaction data, yet collecting it on physical robots is slow and labor-intensive. Recent ego-to-robot pipelines retarget first-person view human videos to robot data via transferring hand and arm motion. They judge fidelity mainly by visual appearance. However, trajectories often fail in terms of physics: fingers hover beside objects, and grippers close on empty space. We argue that how the object moves and the contacts that drive the motion count. Thus, we present Ego2X, an object-centric framework that converts monocular egocentric video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Ego2X centers on CORE (Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation), which records each contact on the object by its surface anchor, as well as relative force, grasp mode, and interaction state. Throughout the pipeline, CORE corrects hand-object drift via object-relative constraints, steers inverse kinematics toward contacts the robot must realize, and preserves held objects during arm erasure and robot compositing. On HOT3D, contact-driven correction reduces in-contact hand depth error by 33.7%, while on EgoDex, contact-driven retargeting realizes 62.9% of annotated contacts, surpassing the official HuRo pipeline (27.9%). In RoboTwin 2.0, post-training X-VLA on Ego2X episodes alone, without simulator demonstrations, raises task success rate from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0% across 200 paired scenes. We will publicly release our conversion pipeline and CORE-annotated dataset for dexterous hands and parallel grippers.

papers.title: Evaluating LIM Trading Agents: A Critical Review of Backtesting Validity and Reporting Practices
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in investment research, and many studies report promising historical returns. However, such results are only credible if researchers can demonstrate that the model used only information available at the time, account for how strategies and configurations were selected, and explain how reported returns were generated. We identify six common threats to validity in LLM investment evaluations and apply them to 18 published studies. Across 108 assessments, we find substantial gaps in reporting. No paper fully addresses information timing, model-memory exposure, universe selection, trading costs, or configuration-selection bias. Only four studies provide minimum evidence that results hold across multiple market periods. Our analysis reveals that commonly used safeguards often address different problems than researchers assume. For example, using dated inputs does not guarantee that a pretrained model lacked knowledge of future events, and repeated experimental runs do not correct for strategy-selection bias. We therefore propose an evaluation protocol for future LLM investment research. Rather than judging whether LLMs can generate profits, our study examines whether existing evidence is sufficient to support such claims. We conclude that current reporting practices are generally insufficient for that purpose.

papers.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly. Here we develop a compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product State (CAMPS) framework that reuses Clifford transformations across shots, recycles qubits released by measurements, evolves a compressed residual state, and accelerates sampling through rotation fusion and compilation tailored to the MPS layout. Surface-code benchmarks under fixed-sign coherent noise yield accurate logical error estimates at small bond dimensions, while random-sign simulations up to distance $d=9$ and on the $[[72,12,6]]$ bivariate bicycle code match the Pauli-twirling approximation results. Compared with uncompiled CAMPS, compiled CAMPS converges at smaller bond dimensions and achieves order-of-magnitude sampling speedups at equal bond dimension, opening a scalable route to studying coherent error propagation in larger fault-tolerant circuits.

papers.title: DORMS: Image Segmentation via Depth-Ordered Region Merge Trees
papers.abstract: We introduce DORMS (Depth-Ordered Region Merging for Segmentation), a purely algorithmic approach to image segmentation from monocular depth maps, requiring no neural networks or learned parameters in the segmentation process. An off-the-shelf monocular depth estimator provides the input depth maps. Our method constructs depth-ordered merge trees through a deterministic union-find sweep, combining component area, depth persistence, and spatial contact constraints to guide region merging. A threshold search determines the segmentation granularity according to a specified target region count, while global depth detrending improves the separation of local geometric structures. Extensive experiments on COCO Panoptic, Cityscapes, and ADE20K demonstrate consistent improvements over classical segmentation baselines and competitive performance against zero-shot neural segmentation models. Notably, our method outperforms all evaluated zero-shot models on Cityscapes, while remaining competitive with several approaches on COCO and ADE20K. These results highlight the potential of purely algorithmic geometric reasoning for image segmentation without learned segmentation models.

papers.title: WAIVES: Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs
papers.abstract: Weak-form methods have transformed inference for deterministic dynamical systems. By integrating the governing equations against smooth, compactly supported test functions, they trade noise-amplifying differentiation for noise-attenuating integration, yielding fast and robust estimates. Extending this idea to stochastic differential equations (SDEs) has proven harder, and a consistent single-trajectory formulation in the time domain has remained out of reach. Applied naively in the time domain, the weak form makes the regressors and the errors functionals of the same noise, creating endogeneity that leaves weak-form least squares biased and inconsistent. We resolve it with instrumental variables, a classical idea from econometrics. Weak-form integrals over nearby disjoint time windows prove to be valid instruments, correlated with the regressors yet uncorrelated with the error, restoring consistency and asymptotic normality. The resulting generalized-method-of-moments estimator, WAIVES (Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs), requires only a linear solve, with no likelihood evaluations, filtering, or simulation. It is therefore an order of magnitude faster than exact-likelihood methods where those exist, and it applies unchanged where they do not, with standard errors and calibrated confidence intervals supplied by the moment conditions. It also separates measurement noise from the intrinsic randomness of the dynamics. Across nine example systems, spanning linear, bistable, chaotic, excitable, state-dependent-diffusion, non-polynomial, hypoelliptic, and high-dimensional regimes (up to 120 dimensions), WAIVES recovers nonlinear drift and diffusion with negligible bias and near-nominal interval coverage. We close with two real-data illustrations: a 167-year North Atlantic sea-surface-temperature record and an optical-tweezer calibration.

papers.title: HETEROVLM: Edge Multi-Request Vision-Language Model Serving on a Heterogeneous Versal SoC with AI Engines and Programmable Logic
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) play a pivotal role in enabling autonomous vehicles and robots to perceive and reason about the physical world. Edge computers in autonomous systems typically serve concurrent VLM inference requests with various deadlines, each mixing a compute-bound encoder and prefill stage with a memory-bound decode stage. GPU serving optimizes for high throughput in datacenters, with per-iteration host scheduling, which can cause an urgent request to wait for a long time, and small-batch decode costs much energy per token. Prior accelerators on Versal AI Engine (AIE) SoCs map one model onto a fixed AIE dataflow graph for one input stream, without decode or request scheduling, which limits their capability in serving multiple requests. We present HETEROVLM, which is optimized for multi-request VLM serving on a resource-constrained heterogeneous platform. It keeps the AIE graph static and makes it schedulable. The AIE array runs the encoder, prefill and attention, and the programmable logic (PL) implements GEMV engines for small decode steps and a scheduler that orders short work units by class and deadline. Concurrent requests share one decode step that reads the weights once. An urgent request preempts at a work-unit boundary, and the paused request resumes from its results in DDR memory. On an AMD Versal VC1902, text and camera questions get their first tokens in 140 and 303 ms. HETEROVLM decodes a single request 1.3x and 4.0x faster than NVIDIA Tesla T4 and Jetson Orin Nano Super GPUs, consuming only 61% and 73% of their energy per token, or 51% of the energy per token of an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti. A single bitstream runs multiple VLMs, switching between them at run time. A demo is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/demo heterovlm-EFM2/.

papers.title: ReflectScene:MLLM-Guided Closed-Loop Diffusion for 3D Indoor Scene Generation
papers.abstract: Text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation requires layouts satisfying geometric, functional, and semantic constraints. However, existing diffusion methods rely primarily on static textual conditions, limiting their ability to assess evolving scenes and translate semantic discrepancies into executable object-level corrections. MLLM-based post-hoc refinement provides semantic feedback but remains decoupled from denoising, potentially disrupting scene coherence. We propose ReflectScene, an MLLM-guided closed-loop diffusion framework. First, we introduce Hierarchical Prior-Grounded Scene Understanding that aligns structured layouts with multi-view visual evidence, to interpret object-specific context and scene global semantics via a frozen multi-modal large language model (MLLM). Second, we propose MLLM-Guided Semantic Reward Evaluation to distill MLLM's diagnoses and assessments on possible candidate corrections into a lightweight Reward Predictor, enabling correction decision making with reduced computation burden. Finally, Decision-Conditioned Trajectory-Consistent Diffusion is proposed to integrate selected corrections through transient conditioning and persistent clean-estimate projection, correcting object layout in the generated scene while preserving non-target arrangements throughout denoising. Experiments on 3D-FRONT demonstrate improved functional consistency and semantic alignment while maintaining competitive generation quality and diversity.

papers.title: Mapping the Design Space of Feature Sampling for Optical Flow
papers.abstract: The computation of correlation features is crucial for optical flow estimation. Existing methods (e.g., RAFT) perform fixed-radius lookups on a cost volume, yielding a set of correlation features for each position; alternatively, WAFT performs single-point feature indexing, yielding one correlation feature vector per position. None of them designs a suitable correlation feature sampling scheme for each position according to regional characteristics. Our insight is that not every position requires the same sampling scheme. Applying an identical sampling scheme to every position is either redundant or insufficient and ignores the specific characteristics of the corresponding region. This paper rethinks the design of feature sampling and investigates the following question: should the support of feature sampling---i.e., the extent and directions over which evidence is aggregated---be learned separately for each query position? To study this question, we propose SAGE (Sampling with Anisotropic Gaussian Expectation). This method replaces single-point sampling with a per-pixel anisotropic Gaussian expectation on a fixed candidate grid centered on the current optical flow estimate. A positive-definite precision matrix controls the scale, anisotropy, and orientation of the sampling support, with single-point sampling included as its limiting case. Consequently, the sampling support becomes an explicit and analyzable design variable and provides a principled way to analyze how directional feature aggregation affects correspondence learning. Extensive experiments show that SAGE, while adding only 1.5% multiply-accumulate operations (MACs), effectively improves zero-shot cross-dataset generalization. When trained only on FlyingChairs and FlyingThings, SAGE reduces the end-point error (EPE) by 24.2% and 16.4% on Sintel clean and final, and reduces KITTI F1-epe and F1-all by 7.2% and 11.6%.

papers.title: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records
papers.abstract: Classical time series analysis converts temporal dependence into structure that can be learned from a single observed trajectory, through stationarity, ergodicity, spectral representation, and finite-memory models. Quantum experiments are naturally time series: every run is a sequence of interventions and outcomes, and the memory of an open system is written in its temporal statistics. However, the classical foundation cannot be translated directly: measuring a process and forgetting the outcome differs from not measuring at all, so no single family of joint probability distributions describes a quantum process. We develop a process-tensor framework for stationary quantum time series and establish its first structural theorems. For stationary combs of finite quantum Markov order l relative to a fixed informationally complete causal break, we construct a finite-dimensional causal transfer map of dimension at most d^{4l}, where d bounds the system Hilbert-space dimension at each step. ... These results supply the stationary foundation on which quantum spectral analysis, model identification, and single-trajectory inference can be built.

papers.title: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents
papers.abstract: General robot manipulation requires both semantic competence and physical foresight. World action models (WAMs) acquire an understanding of and predictive capability over the physical world by jointly modeling visual foresight and action distributions. However, existing WAMs still lack semantic competence: they have limited ability to perform open-world scene understanding, semantic reasoning, and long-horizon planning. Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide these capabilities, effectively integrating their semantic priors into WAM prediction and control remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose CoT-WAM, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework. CoT-WAM uses a learnable embedding to exchange information between the VLM and the WAM, which is supervised by textual and goal-image signals during training to encode rich intent information. A tailored two-stage training strategy enables joint optimization and more effective collaboration between the VLM and WAM. We evaluate CoT-WAM on six benchmarks covering control performance, zero-shot generalization, and long-horizon planning. CoT-WAM achieves SOTA performance on LIBERO, CALVIN, and RoboCasa-Kitchen, and demonstrates stronger zero-shot generalization on LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-Pro without fine-tuning. On RoboCasa365, it further improves long-horizon planning over baselines with and without external planners. Real-world experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in practical deployments. Code is available at: https://github.com/jhz1192/CoT-WAM.git

papers.title: Geometry-bridge flow matching for blind rigid-motion correction in head cone-beam CT
papers.abstract: Rigid motion of a patient head during head cone-beam CT (CBCT) scan can degrade image quality and complicate recovery of accurate anatomical structures from the measured projections. We present a 3D flow-matching prior approach that learns the image changes induced by motion. Its geometry-bridge connects motion-corrupted and motion-free Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructed images of the same source volume through progressively reduced simulated motion. The forward projector's geometry derivative supplies analytic velocity targets along this path. A plug-and-play loop encompasses the learned image updates together with spline-based pose estimation, conjugate-gradient data consistency, and image total-variation regularization. Both the refined image volume and the FDK reconstructed image volume at the estimated poses are evaluated. On simulated 360-view scans from 30 held-out CQ500 patients with nominal per-component motion amplitudes within 10 mm / 10 degrees, the framework achieved state-of-the-art image reconstruction quality and motion accuracy in comparison with other methos such as learned autofocus and diffusion-based joint reconstruction. Mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) reached 37.1 dB and mean detector-plane reprojection error (RPE) was 0.27 mm. With matched endpoints at the inference settings, the geometry bridge improved PSNR by 1.6 dB and reduced RPE by 33% relative to image-linear training. With 50 prior updates and coarse-to-fine motion estimation, total processing time averaged 9.1 minutes per patient on an RTX A6000.

papers.title: Anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test by $e$-spacings
papers.abstract: To perform an anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test, we propose spacing-based \(e\)-processes that control the type-I error rate under arbitrary stopping rules. Based on the maximum spacing of order statistics, we construct spacing-based \(e\)-processes for nonparametrically testing distribution. The resulting procedures are simple and computationally efficient, and are power-consistent. We call them $e$-spacing tests. This approach is especially powerful in detecting localized discrepancy between the data-generating density and the null density. Under mild conditions, the logarithm of the proposed \(e\)-process is asymptotically equivalent to that of the oracle-optimal \(e\)-process. We further generalize the construction from maximal spacing to maximum spacing set in the form of the \(1/k\) fraction of the largest \(m\)th order spacings, as a measure of the lower-level set of density. It boosts power under more global discrepancy from the null. Furthermore, we propose a greedy predictable scheme, via argmax or softmax rules, to combine multiple $e$-spacing testing strategies. We prove that it optimally tunes the $e$-spacing test. The proposed approach is readily generalizable to multivariate testing via a coordinate-wise Rosenblatt-transform. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed methods perform favorably relative to the considered anytime-valid competitors as well as various types of multiple test-adjusted Kolmogorov--Smirnov tests.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X\to C$ be a projective fibration over a curve over a global field. We prove a height inequality for relatively nef adelic line bundles on $X$ whose underlying line bundles are nef. For a nef, relatively ample line bundle over a finitely generated field, we deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model. Over $\mathbb C$, for an ample line bundle and a smooth positive polarization, the Euler--Lagrange equation is the Calabi--Yau equation. On the projective bundle of a vector bundle of degree zero, our energy on quotient metrics agrees with Donaldson's functional when the determinant metric is fixed. We propose a construction of canonical heights on parameter spaces using envelopes of local energies.

papers.title: A Complete Classification of the One-Dimensional Nonlocal Eigenvalue Problem
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the spectral stability of the following one-dimensional nonlocal eigenvalue problem (NLEP) $$ \partial_x^2ϕ-ϕ+pw^{p-1}ϕ-γ(p-1)\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^{r-1}ϕdx}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^r dx}w^p=λϕ, $$ where $w$ is the unique positive even solution of $w''-w+w^p=0$ decaying at infinity, $p,r>1$, and $γ\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\Reγ\ge0$. This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. When $r<(p+3)/2$, the arcs open to the right, and the strictly stable region lies between them. Their common endpoint is $γ=1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ=γ_H>1$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$. In each case, the two arcs approach a common vertical asymptote. As an application, for real $γ\ge0$, the condition for strict spectral stability is $γ>1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ>γ_H$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$, where $γ_H>1$ is the value at which a conjugate pair of eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis. The key ingredient in determining how the number of eigenvalues in the open right half-plane changes at imaginary-axis crossings is a cumulative estimate for the mixed-sign spectral weights that arise for certain $p$ and $r$ with $1<p<3$ and $1<r<2$.

papers.title: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jordán: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

papers.title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
papers.abstract: In weight-space programming, a language model edits a network's weights directly, without gradients. We ask what a successful repair of this kind relies on. We plant faults in the weights of two vision-language models, SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and check each edit made by a coding agent against the original weights. Without being told where to look, the agent finds rescaled projector rows and noise in the vision encoder, infers the unknown scale factors, and returns most or all of the rescaled weights to their exact original values and accuracy to near its original level. These repairs depend on a trace of how the faults were computed. The original weights have 16-bit precision, and faults computed in 32-bit arithmetic leave low bits that only the damaged weights carry, a cue that a real failure need not leave. When we round those bits away, each model answers our test questions as before, but the agent, unaided, no longer repairs either model: on LFM2-VL accuracy recovers by about 4 points, against 17 from the unrounded weights. Marking the damaged weights again in their low bits brings the edits back to them. Rounded weights still hold statistical evidence of the rescaling. On SmolVLM the agent uses it once a sentence in the prompt, which we wrote knowing the fault, names such a statistic; on LFM2-VL, whose scale factors are larger, most sessions find the rescaled rows unaided, but none finds the noise. Swapped rows or columns, which keep the set of stored values, are not found unaided on either model within our budgets. We recommend that studies of weight repair report the number format of the weights and include a rounded control.

papers.title: Topological signatures of criticality: the Ising case
papers.abstract: Topological properties of microscopic configurations may provide additional insight into phase transitions beyond conventional thermodynamic observables. We investigate this idea in the two-dimensional Ising model on square and triangular lattices by associating cell complexes with the positive and negative spin domains and constructing an Euler-characteristic observable from their difference. We provide the expression relating this quantity to conventional observables of the Ising model. This derivation allows us to understand its expected behavior physically. As a byproduct, we show that at any finite positive temperature the expectation of the Euler characteristic exceeds a positive, lattice-size-independent bound, hence disproving a previously suggested conjecture. Monte Carlo simulations combined with multihistogram reweighting show that this spin-odd topological observable exhibits order-parameter-like behavior near the ferromagnetic transition. Finite-size scaling of its susceptibility yields pseudocritical temperatures that converge to the known critical temperature for both lattice geometries. On the square lattice, the leading-order estimate of the critical exponent obtained from the topological observable depends more strongly on the fitting range than the magnetization estimate. This behavior is consistent with stronger subleading finite-size corrections, as supported by fits including an additional correction term. On the triangular lattice, the corresponding estimate remains consistent with the theoretical Ising value. Our study suggests that topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic can provide an alternative way to locate order-disorder phase transitions in the systems considered here. Since the definition of these observables is purely geometrical, they can provide useful insights in cases in which order parameters cannot be constructed.

papers.title: MetaphIR: Corpus-Scale Applicability Analysis for LLVM Peephole Optimizations
papers.abstract: Peephole optimizations replace short source instruction sequences with more efficient equivalents, typically guarded by preconditions such as requiring a constant operand to be a power of two. Since every new rewrite adds maintenance burden and compile-time cost, compiler developers need to know how often real-world programs both match the source pattern and satisfy its preconditions before committing to an implementation. Existing workflows fall short: structural search over an intermediate representation (IR) corpus of 4.8 million functions ignores preconditions and therefore overcounts, whereas implementing the rewrite and recompiling the corpus yields exact counts only after paying the engineering cost, with each run of the corpus's on-demand recompilation pipeline taking a median of 47 minutes. This delay is especially limiting when generalizing a rewrite, as developers often iterate over multiple variants to trade off coverage against complexity. We introduce MetaphIR, a system pairing a domain-specific language for expressing LLVM peephole optimizations with an indexed search engine over large IR corpora. Using a syntax modeled on LLVM's C++ matchers, MetaphIR patterns augment LLVM IR with holes and Boolean preconditions over matched values. To answer queries at interactive speed, MetaphIR builds compact per-function summaries ahead of time and uses abstract interpretation over those summaries to soundly filter out functions that cannot satisfy a query's constraints. Across twenty recent peephole optimizations from LLVM's InstCombine pass, MetaphIR recovers the exact set of functions where each rewrite applies in isolation, achieving 100% precision and recall. Queries complete in a median of 1.27 seconds---a 22x speedup over a full corpus scan---enabling developers to quickly gauge an optimization's reach and generality prior to implementation.

papers.title: Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite Qubit System
papers.abstract: Quantum Computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement of quantum bits (qubits), to represent and manipulate information in multidimensional state spaces. This approach allows complex mathematical functions to be executed simultaneously rather than sequentially, making them much more efficient than classical computers. However, current quantum computers suffer from quantum decoherence, where small changes to their environment, such as thermal fluctuations and vibrations, affect the systems' fragile states. The goal of this study is to discuss the functionality of a proposed Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite qubit system by solving the unitary time-evolution of a quantum state vector for the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and traverse anisotropy terms at temperatures up to 10 K. The system can effectively transfer population between its two lowest states at rates predicted by the Rabi half-period, with 99.9% fidelity. Additionally, it can hold the population at a desired state without docohering. The results remained consistent for temperatures up to 10 K, meaning, unlike many common qubit systems, the proposed qubit system could function without a dilution fridge and is not fragile to thermal noise.

papers.title: RESCUE Jumper: A Centimeter-Scale Rolling and Jumping Robot for Search and Rescue
papers.abstract: Centimeter-scale robots are promising for urban search and rescue because they can enter confined spaces that are inaccessible or unsafe for humans. However, their small size limits obstacle traversal after deployment. This paper presents the RESCUE Jumper, a 125 g mobile robot with a 6.2 cm width and 6.2 cm diameter wheels that combines ground rolling with jumping to traverse steps and gaps that exceeds its rolling capability. The RESCUE Jumper uses its two actuators for both rolling mode and jumping by reversing the direction of wheel motion. Forward wheel motion enables rolling, while reverse wheel motion winds a spring steel tail to store elastic potential energy and release it for jumping. The RESCUE Jumper varies tail winding speed to control jump direction, transitioning from backward to forward jumps as winding speed increases from 0.75 rad/s to 8.73 rad/s. The launch angle of the jumps ranges from 45 degree to -11 degree with respect to the vertical axis, reaching a maximum height of 9.2 cm and a maximum lateral displacement of 11.2 cm. We model the winding speed-dependent jumping behavior in three phases: tail release to determine the contact point and robot orientation, tail straightening until liftoff, and ballistic flight to predict jump height and lateral displacement. Finally, qualitative tests highlight the robot's locomotion in cluttered, real-world environments. The model and experiments presented in this work can inform future designs of space-constrained jump mechanisms in centimeter-scale robots for search and rescue and inspection in unstructured environments.

papers.title: Ramsey Theory for Edge Ideals
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of Ramsey theory for edge ideals. The edge ideal I_G is generated by the monomials x_ux_v for all edges uv of G. A central invariant measuring structure in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra are the betti number beta_{i,j}(S/I) for some ideal I in a ring S. We prove the Ramsey Theorem for Edge Ideals: For any betti number indices i,j, and any number of colors m, there is a graph F such that for every m-coloring of the edges of F, there is a color l such that beta_{i,j}(S/I_{F_l}) >0, where F_l is the subgraph of F whose edges are in color l. Moreover, the number of vertices of F is at most jm^2.

papers.title: Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones
papers.abstract: Compact convolutional backbones such as EfficientNet achieve strong parameter efficiency through local depthwise separable convolutions, yet two structural questions remain central to hybrid design: where does global self-attention improve recognition over pure convolution, and can repeated blocks share weights without losing representational capacity? We investigate both questions on ImageNet-1k (50,000-image validation) using controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments. First, we show that wrapping a classification backbone in multi-scale feature pyramids (BiFPN) fails to outperform a plain MBConv trunk (69.99% - 71.81% vs. 72.86% plain B0) until paired with stage attention (73.15%). In contrast, keeping the MBConv trunk intact and inserting lightweight zero-gated residual self-attention adapters at stages P3 (28x28 windowed), P4 (14x14 global), and P5 (7x7 global) reaches 74.02% standalone and outperforms a bit-for-bit matched plain-B0 control by +0.954 percentage points (73.88% vs. 72.92%) across an 88-epoch stateless replay schedule, with learned attention amplitude rising monotonically with semantic depth (27.2% at P3 -> 45.4% at P4 -> 66.3% at P5). Second, we evaluate recurrent weight sharing across repeated MBConv blocks with pass-specific BatchNorm statistics (+1,536 parameters per pass). While post-hoc kernel averaging degrades accuracy to 17.03% and single-template stage tying (-27.6% parameters) plateaus at 66.10%, alternating two shared block templates ([B1, A, B, A]) in Stage 6 cuts total model parameters by 10.9% (582K weights) and recovers by +10.82 points in a single epoch to 70.92% (-1.84 points vs. unshared control).

papers.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
papers.abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage pointwise projections and depthwise layers. Second, we introduce a structured, multi-step recovery waterfall that evaluates selective integer precision (INT4/INT8) and selective floating-point scales. We show that keeping less than 5% of critical layer activations in 8-bit precision recovers up to 92% of the accuracy lost during aggressive sub-4-bit compression. Finally, we bridge the hardware reality gap by evaluating deployment performance on standard ARM and x86 CPU architectures. We show that while low-bit quantization reduces memory storage requirements, standard runtime software bit-unpacking introduces a 1.48x to 21.5x execution slowdown depending on batch size, highlighting a critical trade-off between model footprint and actual edge throughput. Our findings provide a practical blueprint for navigating the limits of sub-4-bit deployment without sacrificing hardware performance.

papers.title: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

papers.title: Lunar laser ranging analyses of NGLR-1 data with PEP and prospects for MPAc: towards one millimeter range precision
papers.abstract: Since 1969, Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) has provided critical data for investigating Earth-Moon dynamics, lunar internal structure, and tests of General Relativity (GR). However, the measurement precision of historical arrays (such as those from Apollo and Lunokhod missions) is inherently limited by laser pulse broadening induced by lunar librations. To overcome this limit, next-generation single Cube Corner Retroreflectors (CCRs) of large optical diameter have been developed to eliminate pulse dispersion, enabling LLR measurements to advance from centimeter-level precision down to the millimeter scale. In this work, we present a detailed analysis of LLR observations from NGLR-1 (Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector-1), the first single 10cm-diameter CCR deployed on the lunar surface. Carried out using the Planetary Ephemeris Program (PEP), this study investigates individual range measurements, normal points (NPs), residuals, and observational dispersion collected by the ground stations at Apache Point Observatory Lunar laser ranging station (APOL), Wettzell, and Grasse. The results: demonstrate the success of NGLR-1 in significantly enhancing time of flight measurement precision compared to legacy Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector arrays; indicate similar good prospects also for ESA's MPAc laser retroreflector (MoonLIGHT with Pointing Actuators) to be launched in early 2027; pave the way for a new era of LLR observations and enhanced tests of GR, alternative gravity theories in general and improved lunar geophysics and geodesy.

papers.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
papers.abstract: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers. Recent designs commonly use a separate n-gram embedding table for each layer, which makes the tables costly in memory and prevents layers from sharing what they learn. However, a single shared table gives every layer the same embedding, leaves no room for layer-wise preferences, and performs poorly in practice. We propose Chorus, in which one set of n-gram embedding tables serves the whole network and every layer reads it in its own way. Each layer maps the refined embedding through its own projection layer, after rescaling its components by factors computed from its current hidden state. Chorus matches the quality of existing n-gram methods with 87% smaller tables: with 1.2B table parameters it predicts text better than FactorEngram and DeepSeek's Engram do with 9.6B. It outperforms Engram, TN-gram and FactorEngram in every setting where we compared them, across table sizes from 20M to 9.6B parameters. We also show that the recently proposed memory-efficient optimizer Ember works well with Chorus, saving 99.2% of table-optimizer memory compared with AdamW without degrading training performance. These results enable further scaling of n-gram embedding tables along the table-size axis by reducing memory use and allowing shared knowledge to be reused across layers.

papers.title: Asymmetric Optical Image Watermarking
papers.abstract: Watermark detectors held by a provider cannot be checked by third parties, and a party that can detect a mark can usually also forge it. We study a two-layer image watermark in which the Fourier transform at the core of the pipeline is performed by a coherent optical 4F unit. Layer 1 carries an Ed25519 signature bound to the image content in Fourier magnitudes, so anyone with the public key verifies offline. Layer 2 is a key-defined carrier written by a secret phase hologram and read by a matched-filter correlator. The optics is a scalar-diffraction simulation with finite modulator bits, pixel aperture, pupil, defocus, misalignment, and sensor noise. No hardware is built. All criteria were fixed in a hashed specification before any optical result. The simulated optical signer reproduces the digital pipeline (field error 1.7e-15, bit agreement 99.997%), verifies at least 99.5% of 877 images under each of 8 post-sensor settings, one unattacked, and accepts none of 40,670 unmarked images. The optical carrier is key-selective: the matched key detects it on 99.8% of the unattacked images, and detection falls to 0% under a scale error of 1% and to 0% under a mask shift of 1 bin. Security rests on the signature and the content binding, for which we separate what is provable from what is measured.

papers.title: Global genetic inference at the scale of mass disasters
papers.abstract: DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. Joint analysis avoids this dependence on decision order, but combinatorial growth has historically made it prohibitive in large cases. In this paper, we show that the general joint identification problem is NP-hard and develop a local-to-global framework for joint genetic inference at scale. We reduce the search using genetic compatibility tests, likelihood-based pruning of unlikely assignments, and symmetry reductions. We represent pedigree likelihoods as polynomials and reformulate the Elston-Stewart algorithm for efficient parallel likelihood evaluation on GPUs. Together, these advances yield a manageable set of candidate assignments and their likelihoods, from which we construct an integer linear program that resolves competing identifications and determines the global maximum-likelihood assignment. In small benchmarks, the method recovers the exhaustive-search optimum with up to 99.96% fewer likelihood evaluations. We also apply it to simulated disasters involving up to 10 thousand victims and missing persons. The framework is not limited to a single global optimum but yields a list of probable alternative assignments, thus providing a flexible tool to be used alongside other forensic evidence.

papers.title: A Two-Spectrum Deterministic Equivalent for Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
papers.abstract: Rank-one perturbations of the mean characteristic polynomial of a random skew-kernel matrix assign a positive spatial weight to each root. For independent centered isotropic rows, the resulting response tracks the sample almost surely against each deterministic spatial test, uniformly over positive scales and arbitrary inputs, exactly when row energies concentrate on common projections of proportional rank. Directional absolute first moments determine this condition. The determinant Jensen gap controls the spatial response in every real orthonormal basis. For identity spatial covariance, logarithmic derivatives of the mean determinant give the temporal weights of the row energies it detects. Flat kernels of one prescribed rank suffice to test the row condition. A scalar equation in the two input spectra approximates the matrix response of the roots within $4/d$ in normalized trace norm. A varying ordinary response and the same-scale overlap of independent samples recover both input laws up to reciprocal rescaling, with Lipschitz stability of the relative spatial parameter and an optimal logarithmic modulus for the compactified laws on intervals of positive variation. Brownian area gives explicit spatial half-Cauchy mixtures.

papers.title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels
papers.abstract: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding on one quarter of its dimensions. The Gemma 4 report states that this design reduces the global KV cache by up to 37.5%, but the open serving engines that we checked still store a full key and a full value: 1,024 values per KV head and token. We store one 640-value row instead, exact in real arithmetic, and an unchanged paged attention kernel reads it through two overlapping strided views as its key cache and its value cache. In a vLLM prototype with the 16-bit 31B model, the outputs are bit-identical to an emulation of the same arithmetic on the stock cache, 2 of 432 final answers differ from the stock engine (within its run-to-run noise), and the steady decode KV memory per request falls by a factor of 1.34 to 1.40 at 32K to 64K tokens. On a prefill/decode pair of two A100 GPUs with NIXL transfer and CPU offload, a decode engine with a full 15 GiB pool ran 1.38 times the stock decode tokens per step for 16K-token prompts (repeated to 0.06%) and 1.24 times for 8K-token prompts; a model of the vLLM block pool predicted both ratios to within 1% (the engine was 0.7% to 0.9% higher) and matched the change between them. The eager decode throughput rose by 1.30 and 1.11 times, and on this path the compact engine gave the same output tokens as the emulation for 8 prompts at batch 1. The run-time prototype makes an eager step 4% to 9% slower at equal batch, and the method does not yet stack with an 8-bit KV cache at the default scale.

papers.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can correctly interpret physics diagrams yet apply constraints outside the states or conditions in which they hold, causing premise errors to propagate through subsequent calculations. We introduce PhysScope, an inference-time visual harness that supports self-correction of these scope mismatches without updating model weights. PhysScope enables the model to link physical scopes directly to its visual observations and explicitly constructs derived views to support reasoning. The harness imposes explicit constraints on state distinctions, conditions, and physical scopes during model reasoning, and checks agent-proposed revisions against sources and scopes. Accepted revisions invalidate registered dependents, thereby maintaining scope-aware working memory. On PhysAlign, PhysScope achieves higher solving scores than direct solving across all six evaluated VLMs. With Gemini-3.8-flash, it outperforms Canvas-CoT by 9.34 percentage points and substantially improves solving accuracy on the out-of-distribution (OOD) PhysUniBench benchmark. Ablation studies support explicit scope management and dependency maintenance as design principles for multimodal physics reasoning agents.

papers.title: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
papers.abstract: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A. Hanlon, J. Hicks, and O. Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

papers.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
papers.abstract: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce MakoBORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. MakoBORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, MakoBORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, MakoBORN finishes in 1.41 h on a single CPU node, 77$\times$ faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline and still 9.8$\times$ faster with development time included. On a single GPU, MakoBORN completes the ubiquitin calculation in 2.1 h, the same order of runtime as the GPU-accelerated package Mako on 64 GPUs, and shortens the B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1 h (173$\times$).

papers.title: PCRG: Training-Free Pruning and Caching of Reference Tokens for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Reference-to-video diffusion transformers pack the variational autoencoder (VAE) latents of all references and the generated tokens into one full-attention sequence, in which reference tokens make up about half. Because attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length, these tokens take up an even larger share of the attention computation, yet most of them are static, smooth or irrelevant to the output. To accelerate reference-conditioned generation, we propose pruning and caching of reference tokens for video generation (PCRG), a training-free, plug-and-play method that uses two signals the model already computes to assign each reference token to one of three tiers, namely pruned, cached or kept. The first is a low-level redundancy r from VAE latents, since a token whose latent barely changes over time or across its neighbors adds little new content. The second is a high-level importance g from the vision-language-model (VLM) conditioner, where the attention that the prompt and any first or last frames pay to a token tells whether the output needs to read it. Tokens that are not redundant are kept, and redundant tokens are cached if important and pruned otherwise. Pruned tokens leave the sequence before the first step with all rotary position embedding positions unchanged. Cached tokens have their keys and values computed once and reused, and kept tokens are processed as usual. On MiniMax-H3, already distilled to 8 timesteps and quantized to int8, PCRG is 1.57x faster end to end on our V2V-Bench and 1.49x faster on the public VACE-Benchmark, while the quality of VBench drops by only 0.24% and 0.17%, respectively. PCRG shortens the sequence rather than changing how attention is computed or which steps are run, so it also stacks on step caching and sparse attention. On V2V-Bench it reaches 1.86x with TeaCache, 1.82x with Spark at nearly unchanged fidelity and 2.15x with Veda.

papers.title: Proven optimality for LABS with quantum-classical branch and bound
papers.abstract: Low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) are the phase codes of pulse compression radar and the synchronization words of digital communication, and finding the sequence of a given length whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the smallest sum of squares is a hard binary optimization problem. The quantum optimization methods tested on LABS so far return good sequences, but they cannot show that a sequence is optimal or bound how far from optimal it may be. We show that a quantum optimization algorithm can deliver proven optimality. In our quantum-classical branch and bound, fixed-angle QAOA samples the Hamiltonians of the nodes of the search tree, its samples supply candidate sequences and the branching choice, and classical bounds prune the tree, so that the algorithm returns either a proof of optimality or, if it is stopped early, the best sequence found with a certified lower bound and gap. It works on the native quartic Hamiltonian without penalty terms, and its correctness does not depend on the sampler. With QAOA at depth p= 12 and at p= 1 and 1,000 shots per node, it proved the optima of all lengths from 2 to 30, where from length 27 on the root node is split without being sampled. Every run records both bounds against time, and its primal-dual integral measures its convergence. We claim no speedup.

papers.title: Classification of Tissues on MALDI-MSI Image Modality for Pancreatic Cancer Studies
papers.abstract: Mass Spectrometry Imaging (MSI) spatially maps molecular distributions in tissue sections. Despite the availability of preprocessing tools for MSI data, building end-to-end workflows suitable for deep learning remains challenging. We have developed a fully automated pipeline for transformation of raw Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) data into deep-learning-ready image patches for binary pancreatic tissue classification (tumoral vs non-tumoral) and built individual models for recognition of tumoral regions in spectral images. Images resulting from the proposed pipeline and from reference interactive workflow are very close in terms of image quality metric mean squared error (MSE). The proposed pipeline computational time is of 20 min in average compared to a full working day of the reference interactive workflow. The models achieved 0.94 accuracy on high-resolution spectra and a mean accuracy of 0.59 on lower-resolution spectra.

papers.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
papers.abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. This study introduces a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking CPG model embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop. A composite synchronization metric is developed, integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. Its performance is evaluated across systematically varied stimulation waveforms and synaptic configurations. Statistical analysis reveals that stimulation type dominates regime determination, with tonic drive yielding the most robust antiphase synchronization. Periodic inputs induce nonlinear saturation and context-dependent network routing. Although synaptic weights alone show limited discriminative power, they significantly modulate robustness within a given stimulation context, with reciprocal Ia interneuron connections emerging as key stabilizers. The proposed composite metric achieves robust antiphase detection, outperforming traditional phase-only measures while preserving biophysical interpretability. These findings establish a statistically validated, hierarchical modeling approach in which external drive defines the operating regime and targeted synaptic configurations fine-tune dynamic stability, providing actionable guidelines for closed-loop neuromechanical controllers and adaptive neuroprosthetic interfaces.

papers.title: CheckCo: Checkpoint-Coordinated Load Balancing for Skewed Event Streams at Scale
papers.abstract: Event streams are rarely uniform: a few dominant keys can generate orders of magnitude more events than the rest, overloading the workers that receive them and capping throughput. We present CheckCo, a checkpoint-coordinated load-balancing algorithm built on a dynamic oracle that estimates per-key frequencies from the live stream, with no prior statistics. Workers count events per key locally; at each checkpoint barrier, the counts are merged into a partitioning function that divides each key into a number of splits roughly proportional to its estimated frequency and packs the splits onto workers, and this function routes the next checkpoint window. We derive approximation bounds on the resulting load imbalance from classical scheduling results and bound its total key fan-out. On a production pipeline processing over 100 billion events per day, the most loaded worker receives only 9.8% more events than the average over a day (imbalance ratio 1.10), against 8.03 for key-based routing in simulation; in simulation, CheckCo also needs less than half the fan-out of earlier partitioners that reach comparable balance. Shifts in the key distribution are reflected in routing from the next checkpoint on, and the load stays balanced through job restarts.

papers.title: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
papers.abstract: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. The unprecedented spectral resolution of XRISM/Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even at small scale, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim, some in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 Msol sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. Overall the best agreement is found for models with a too high metallicity to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronisation such as carbon simmering for Chandrasekhar mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar mass, double detonation models with a WD mass lower than 1Msol are suggested.

papers.title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
papers.abstract: Fast System-1 models enable responsive actions but struggle with complex or unfamiliar tasks. Large language model (LLM)-based System-2 provides strong reasoning capabilities, yet repeated invocation incurs substantial latency and computational costs. To bridge this gap, we propose JevRSI, a System-1/System-2 collaboration framework that transforms LLM reasoning into transferable decision support through recursive harness improvement. A Jev-style System-1 model enables low-latency action selection, while an asynchronous System-2 LLM develops a modular harness. The harness integrates procedures, state memory, and world models to provide decision contexts spanning the past, present, and future. Utility-driven retrieval selects modules based on both contextual relevance and their utility on previous tasks. Environmental feedback guides targeted revisions and enables recursive self-improvement. Experiments across three datasets show that JevRSI consistently improves decision quality, matching or surpassing LLM agents in several settings. It preserves low-latency execution with favorable performance-cost trade-offs. Moreover, System-2 development interventions decrease as the harness evolves, amortizing System-2 costs through continuous improvement. Our project is available at https://github.com/usail-hkust/JevRSI.

papers.title: Projection of global daily CO2 emissions in 2026
papers.abstract: Global fossil-fuel combustion and industrial-process CO2 emissions remain close to historical highs, yet the recent slowdown in growth is difficult to assess before conventional inventories become available. We project emissions for 2026 and examine daily departures during major climate and energy disruptions. We fit Prophet models to the latest five years of Carbon Monitor activity estimates for 47 region-sector series. We use these models to project daily emissions for October-December and combine them with activity estimates through September. Global emissions are estimated at 38.0 Gt CO2 in 2026, 34.1 Mt CO2 (-0.1%) below 2025. The hindcast-adjusted range for the annual change is -0.9% to +0.7%. Five September-cutoff hindcasts show lower mean daily errors and larger mean absolute annual biases for Prophet than for a seasonal-naive benchmark. Regional increases total 0.331 Gt and decreases total 0.365 Gt, so 95.1% of the 0.696 Gt gross movement cancels in the global sum. China contributes the largest reduction (-0.243 Gt), concentrated in industry and ground transport, whereas India contributes the largest increase (+0.222 Gt), led by power and industry. Heat-period power anomalies differ among countries and can be muted by summer averaging, while aviation and shipping show different disruption and recovery profiles. Resolving the near-zero global change reveals where reductions are concentrated and where continued growth offsets them, providing a timely basis for assessing the breadth of mitigation progress.

papers.title: SIDUMN: Self-Supervised Image Denoising Under Symmetric Multiplicative Noise
papers.abstract: Self-supervised denoising is challenging when the corruption is multiplicative and signal-dependent. In this letter, we propose SIDUMN, a symmetric noisier framework for self-supervised denoising under mean-one symmetric multiplicative noise. Given noisy observations and the noise law, the method samples an independent synthetic noise factor from the same law and constructs two complementary noisier images by applying the factor and its reflection about one. The denoising network is trained to predict one noisier image from the other, and at inference the reconstructions of $K$ such antithetic pairs are averaged. We show that the population target of the training loss is the clean conditional mean minus a multiplicative cross-term. We further prove that, for any trained network, antithetic averaging never increases the expected squared error of a single noisier-input reconstruction. Numerical results validate the theoretical findings and the proposed method.

papers.title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
papers.abstract: A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved. However, very few results are known for graphs with maximum degree four or more. Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana showed that every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{19})$-packing edge-coloring and a $(1^2,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. In this paper, we improve the results of Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana by showing every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. As a corollary of our result, every graph with degree at most four has a $(1^2,2^{16})$-packing edge-coloring.

papers.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point.
